The model generates testable predictions for borrower-bank matched lending, financially constrained borrowers, mandate-bound banks, and the staggered implementation of European disclosure rules across countries.

detail.abstract: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation has emerged as an effective paradigm for alleviating the reliance on dense expert annotations. However, most existing methods primarily depend on output-level consistency regularization and pseudo-label supervision, while paying insufficient attention to representation discrepancies between heterogeneous networks in the intermediate feature space. Moreover, the lack of coordinated multi-scale feature modeling limits their ability to simultaneously capture fine-grained local details and global anatomical semantics, particularly in anatomically complex regions with ambiguous boundaries. To address these limitations, we propose FRMC, a semi-supervised medical image segmentation framework that integrates Feature-Regularized Mutual Consistency with Multi-scale Contrastive Enhancement in a heterogeneous dual-network architecture. Specifically, we develop a Feature-level Cross-regularization Mechanism (FCM) to explicitly mitigate latent representation discrepancies between heterogeneous branches. By applying region-constrained feature masking and projecting multi-level features into a shared normalized embedding space, this mechanism enforces feature-level semantic consistency and enhances the reliability of pseudo-label learning. Furthermore, we introduce a Multi-scale Contrastive Enhancement Strategy (MCES) to improve feature discriminability across hierarchical semantic levels. Through adaptive response-aware weighting and cross-model contrastive learning on aligned multi-scale representations, this strategy facilitates the joint modeling of local texture patterns and global anatomical structures, thereby strengthening structural semantic representation and suppressing pseudo-label noise accumulation. Extensive experiments on multiple medical image segmentation benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FRMC. In particular, on the LAHeart dataset with only 20% labeled data, FRMC outperforms strong competing methods by approximately 2 percentage points in Dice score and achieves superior performance on boundary-sensitive metrics, including Hausdorff distance.

title: Managing Public Health Surveillance Operations with Endogenous Population Growth
affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), , Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Antai College of Economics and Management, Sun Yat-sen University and Columbia University - School of Nursing

detail.title: Managing Public Health Surveillance Operations with Endogenous Population Growth

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Public health surveillance is "the continuous, systematic collection, analysis and interpretation of health-related data" to guide public health actions (WHO 2012). In addition to traditional recruitment approaches, such as facility-based methods and community outreach, modern surveillance efforts increasingly rely on social media and online platforms. A central operational challenge in these efforts is recruiting a sufficient number of participants within a targeted time frame to ensure unbiased estimation of population health status. In this paper, we develop a Markov Decision Process model to support decision-making in participant recruitment and service for public health surveillance. The resulting formulation is analytically challenging for several reasons. First, population growth, and consequently participant arrivals, are endogenous to the manager's decisions. Second, the terminal penalty depends on cumulative recruitment outcomes from previous periods, creating strong intertemporal dependencies. Third, the model jointly accounts for multiple sources of uncertainty including time-dependent arrival rates, eligibility rates and attrition rates. To address these challenges, we devise a simple yet powerful exact reformulation of the original model. This reformulation reveals the hidden convexity and submodularity properties that are not apparent in the natural formulation. Leveraging these structural properties, we establish that the optimal population expansion decisions exhibit monotonicity and bounded sensitivity with respect to the system state. Building on these theoretical insights, we develop a highly effective, easy-to-implement, and interpretable heuristic policy to dynamically make population expansion decisions. Using data from a large-scale epidemiological study designed to assess HIV risks, we demonstrate that our approach can substantially improve recruitment efficiency and reduce associated costs by 67.44% compared with the policy currently used in practice.

title: Self-Cannibalizing Flexibility: When Battery Cycling Destroys Future Opportunities
affiliations: University of Macau, University of Macau and New York University (NYU) - Department of Information, Operations, and Management Sciences

detail.title: Self-Cannibalizing Flexibility: When Battery Cycling Destroys Future Opportunities
detail.abstract: Problem definition: Grid-scale batteries profit by charging when electricity is cheap and discharging when it is expensive. But large batteries face a paradox: by exploiting a price spread today, they can weaken the spread opportunities available tomorrow. We call this effect self-cannibalizing flexibility. We study how this dynamic feedback should change cycle timing, project scale, and portfolio coordination. Methodology/results: We develop a tractable two-window cycle-depth model in which battery cycling affects both current prices and the profitability of the next operating opportunity. The model shows that an operator may optimally skip a profitable current cycle when exercising it destroys a more valuable future opportunity. Stronger feedback reduces total repeated cycling but makes operation more selective, concentrating activity in the better window. As capacity expands, use of a weaker window can decline even while total throughput and project value increase. Future uncertainty always raises continuation value, but it can either increase or decrease current waiting depending on whether future exercise is likely to be underused or capacity-constrained. Fragmented operators cycle earlier than an integrated portfolio because they do not fully internalize the future opportunities their actions destroy. Extensions incorporate physical inventory carryover and multiple connected operating windows, and a CAISO-grounded numerical analysis illustrates the economic magnitudes. Managerial implications: The results translate spread cannibalization into practical operating and investment rules. We derive feedback-adjusted bidding thresholds, cycle-selection rules, project-sizing corrections, and portfolio coordination mechanisms, while identifying the data needed to estimate horizon-specific feedback. The central message is simple: a battery should be valued not only for the spread it captures, but also for the future spread its operation destroys.

title: The Tech Synthesis: Artificial Intelligence, Indigenous Purpose, and the Future of Ghanaian Social Enterprises

detail.title: The Tech Synthesis: Artificial Intelligence, Indigenous Purpose, and the Future of Ghanaian Social Enterprises
detail.abstract:
Essays like this one often treat indigenous knowledge as a kind of cultural garnish, a
respectful nod before moving on to the real business of technology and economics. That
treatment misunderstands what indigenous knowledge is and what it does. Far from a
static archive of folklore waiting to be digitised, it is a living, adaptive way of knowing and
deciding that continues to generate real economic and social value today.
A University of Ghana study of the informal economy found that indigenous knowledge
significantly enhances food security, health, and community well-being, and promotes environmental sustainability through resource conservation and waste reduction, with recognition scores in the high seventies to mid-eighties across these areas.

title: Digital Appointment Scheduling in the Registries of Criminal Courts of Appeal in Greece

detail.title: Digital Appointment Scheduling in the Registries of Criminal Courts of Appeal in Greece
detail.abstract: The day-to-day operation of the registries of Criminal Courts of Appeal in Greece is characterized by high volumes of citizens and lawyers seeking in-person services, significant fluctuations in workload, and frequent interruptions to internal administrative tasks. This article examines the potential introduction of a digital appointment scheduling system as a means of improving the organization and delivery of public-facing court services. Drawing on an analysis of current practices, international experience, and the specific characteristics of the Greek criminal justice system, the article proposes a hybrid implementation model that combines scheduled appointments for selected administrative procedures with the continued availability of flexible channels for direct access. It highlights the expected benefits for citizens, lawyers, court administrative staff, and court administration, while also identifying the main conditions required for effective implementation, including regulatory clarity, technical simplicity, and appropriate organizational change management. Finally, the article proposes the pilot implementation of such a system in Greek Criminal Courts of Appeal as a cautious and practical pathway towards a gradual transition to a more predictable and efficient model of court administration.

title: Examining The Value Relevance of Accounting Information: Evidence from Nairobi Stock Exchange (Nse)
affiliations: , Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics, Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics, Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics and University of Jos, Nigeria

detail.title: Examining The Value Relevance of Accounting Information: Evidence from Nairobi Stock Exchange (Nse)
detail.abstract: Prior studies indicate that with the transition of economy from industrial to a technology-driven service-oriented economy, the usefulness of accounting numbers, especially earnings, has reduced. This is shown by the obscurity of the link between market stock prices in accounting figures, especially earnings. Based on his perspective, this study examines the extent of stock price movement explained by the change in key accounting metrics using companies listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. The sample comprises 56 listed companies across 23 sectors from 2016 to 2023. Using a panel data fixed effects regression, we examine the impacts of key accounting metrics on market share prices. We find that both (lnEPS β = 0.137; p < 0.05) and (lnDPS β = 0.331; p < 0.01) have statistically significant positive relationships with share prices in the market (lnMSP). In contrast, lnOCF (β = 0.01, p < 0.1) and lnTA (β = 0.013, p < 0.1) have positive but insignificant impact effects. The R-squared of the model is 0.471, indicating that the four accounting variables explain 47.1 % of the movement in stock price. The findings align with the Dividend Signaling Theory and the Bird-in-Hand Theory. Additionally, the findings show the existence of a weak-form efficient market in the Nairobi Stock Exchange. Generally, the study confirms the persistence of accounting information's value relevance in equity investments in Kenya.

title: Personal AI Sovereignty: From Platform Data Extraction to User-Controlled Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Personal AI Sovereignty: From Platform Data Extraction to User-Controlled Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: Contemporary digital services generally organise personal information around institutional ownership, centralised platforms and repeated data extraction. Individuals may generate enormous quantities of behavioural, social, educational, financial, health and conversational data while retaining limited practical control over how those data are combined, inferred from, transferred or monetised. The emergence of persistent personal artificial intelligence creates an opportunity to reverse this relationship. This paper proposes personal AI sovereignty: an architecture in which an individual controls a persistent AI environment and the underlying longitudinal personal record, while third parties receive only the information required for an authorised purpose. The proposed architecture combines a personal encrypted data environment, self-sovereign identity, verifiable credentials, selective disclosure, zero-knowledge proofs and an auditable permission layer. Sensitive personal content—including journals, health information, photographs, documents and other high-dimensional records—would remain off-chain in encrypted storage. Distributed ledgers would not be used as a database for intimate information; their proposed role is narrower: recording permissions, proofs, credential status, governance rules and auditable access events where appropriate. This distinction is essential because public transparency and personal privacy are not the same objective. The paper argues that data sovereignty should be understood not merely as a privacy preference but as an institutional design principle. The individual should be able to decide who may access information, for what purpose, for how long, under what conditions, and whether access can subsequently be revoked. Service providers should be able to request a verifiable claim without necessarily learning the underlying data—for example, proving that a person is over a required age without revealing a full date of birth. Contemporary standards and public infrastructure demonstrate that significant components of this architecture are already technically and institutionally plausible. W3C Verifiable Credentials 2.0 is a web standard, W3C's Decentralized Identifier work provides a framework for decentralised identity, and European digital identity work incorporates selective disclosure and zero-knowledge techniques. The paper does not claim that blockchain, self-sovereign identity or cryptography automatically solve surveillance, discrimination or commercial exploitation. Technical systems can fail, users can be coerced, metadata can leak, credentials can be abused and governance can be captured. The proposal is therefore a socio-technical architecture: technical sovereignty must be combined with legal rights, transparent governance, independent audit, interoperability, security, accessibility and meaningful user control. The AI Journal is used as a concrete case through which the architecture can be tested, beginning with privacy-preserving child safeguarding and life-course personal development. The wider proposition is that personal AI could shift the dominant digital relationship from platform-owned data extraction to individual data stewardship, creating a foundation for new forms of social coordination without requiring a central institution to possess everyone's personal history.

title: From Watchdog to Policy Participant: Why Retraction Watch and the Center for Scientific Integrity Fail the Test for Presumptive Independent Authority
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: From Watchdog to Policy Participant: Why Retraction Watch and the Center for Scientific Integrity Fail the Test for Presumptive Independent Authority
detail.abstract: Retraction Watch is a journalism website and the Center for Scientific Integrity (CSI) is its private nonprofit parent. Neither label establishes scientific, adjudicative or policy authority. This article tests whether the public record demonstrates the independence, methodological validation, conflict control, external mandate and contestability required for institutions to defer to their outputs. It does not. The resulting conclusion is disqualification from presumptive independent authority: their statements may be examined as claims, but journals, universities, funders, lawmakers and data users should not treat them as verified findings without independent primary-source review.

title: How Much does the Same Orthopedic Implant Cost? A Nationwide Analysis of Price Variation, Competition, Market Concentration, and Procurement Efficiency in Brazil
affiliations: Hospital das Clinicas da Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de  São Paulo. HC-FMUSP, Hospital das Clinicas da Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de  São Paulo. HC-FMUSP, Hospital das Clinicas da Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de  São Paulo. HC-FMUSP and Santa Catarina Federal University

detail.title: How Much does the Same Orthopedic Implant Cost? A Nationwide Analysis of Price Variation, Competition, Market Concentration, and Procurement Efficiency in Brazil

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Background Orthopedic implants are high-cost, clinician-sensitive technologies bought in fragmented, opaque markets. Brazil combines a universal health system with decentralized procurement and newly open national contracting data. We quantified national price variation for clinically equivalent implants and the procurement factors associated with lower prices. Methods We assembled a national cohort of public procurement for orthopedic implants (Jan 1, 2024–June 30, 2026) from PNCP and Compras.gov.br, covering 28 implant families, 112 exact-equivalence codes, and all 27 federative units. Using exact-product fixed-effects log-linear models with buyer-clustered robust SEs, we estimated adjusted price associations, modelled failed or deserted tenders, calculated supplier concentration (HHI), and estimated savings under four benchmarking scenarios. Prices were standardized to June 2026 BRL using the IPCA. Findings Among 14 520 procedures, 12 577 were awarded (26 729 item records; 1 301 866 units; R$5.04 billion). The median exact-product P90:P10 price ratio was 3.77, and eight families were highly concentrated (HHI ≥2500). Each additional bidder was associated with a 3.9% lower price (95% CI 3.6–4.1) and doubling quantity with 6.4% lower (6.0–6.8); price-registration systems (−8.5%) and centralization (−9.3%) with lower prices. Direct contracting (+31.7%), emergency procurement (+36.7%), consignment or instrument loan (+12.6%), imported status (+12.0%), and concentration (+12.6% per 1000 HHI) were associated with higher prices. Conservative benchmarking implied R$1.13 billion (22.4%) in potential savings. Interpretation In a universal health system, competition, aggregation, and transparent exact-product benchmarking were associated with substantially lower implant prices, with potential savings exceeding one fifth of expenditure. Because the design is observational, these associational findings support a national implant price observatory to strengthen procurement stewardship while preserving clinical choice.

title: Sunshine-Induced Sentiment and Consumer Behaviors: New Evidence from Transaction-level Payments
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics, Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) and

detail.title: Sunshine-Induced Sentiment and Consumer Behaviors: New Evidence from Transaction-level Payments
detail.abstract: This research investigates the casual impact of sunshine-induced sentiment on consumer behaviors by leveraging a novel high-frequency dataset of daily city-level weather conditions and individual transaction-level expenditures across over 100 categories in China. We document a sunshine effect: a one okta decrease in the same-day local sky cover is associated with a 0.09% increase in the daily total spending, which aggregates to an additional USD 12 billion in national annual expenditure after controlling for other weather conditions. This effect can be accounted for by an over-optimism mechanism. This sunshine effect is driven by non-discretionary rather than discretionary spending, suggesting that improved mood from sunshine leads consumers to spend more on necessities instead of impulsive purchases of non-essentials. Additionally, the effect is more pronounced among female consumers, those with lower wealth scores, and those with lower education levels. Finally, we also observe a significant but smaller positive effect on daily consumption frequency.

title: Novel Adjuvant-Based Approaches for Overcoming Antibiotic Resistance: A Comprehensive Review
affiliations: and Osmania University

detail.title: Novel Adjuvant-Based Approaches for Overcoming Antibiotic Resistance: A Comprehensive Review

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Antibiotic resistance has emerged as one of the most significant global public health threats, compromising the effectiveness of existing antimicrobial therapies and increasing morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. The rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), and pan-drug-resistant (PDR) bacterial pathogens has intensified the need for innovative therapeutic strategies beyond the development of new antibiotics. Antibiotic adjuvants have gained considerable attention as a promising approach to restore the efficacy of conventional antibiotics by targeting bacterial resistance mechanisms rather than directly exerting antibacterial activity. These adjuvants enhance antibiotic performance through diverse mechanisms, including inhibition of β-lactamases, suppression of efflux pumps, disruption of biofilms, modulation of bacterial membrane permeability, interference with quorum sensing, and attenuation of virulence factors. Recent advances in nanotechnology, natural products, antimicrobial peptides, bacteriophage-derived agents, and CRISPR-based systems have further expanded the potential of adjuvant-based therapies for combating antimicrobial resistance. This review comprehensively discusses the molecular basis of antibiotic resistance, the classification and mechanisms of antibiotic adjuvants, recent technological innovations, and their therapeutic applications against clinically important resistant pathogens and emphasizing future perspectives. Collectively, adjuvant-based approaches represent a promising strategy to extend the lifespan of existing antibiotics and address the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance.

title: Clinical Judgment Under Digital Uncertainty: Information Environments, Telemedicine, and Diagnostic Escalation
affiliations: University of California

detail.title: Clinical Judgment Under Digital Uncertainty: Information Environments, Telemedicine, and Diagnostic Escalation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests that could have influenced the preparation or conclusions of this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding agency.

detail.abstract: Digital healthcare has expanded the quantity, speed, and accessibility of medically relevant information while simultaneously changing the conditions under which clinicians interpret it. Telemedicine, patient portals, search engines, social media, wearable devices, and conversational systems now participate in different stages of the diagnostic process. This article examines how these environments affect clinical judgment under uncertainty, with particular attention to diagnostic escalation. The central problem is not simply misinformation or technological error. It is the interaction between incomplete clinical signals, abundant decontextualized information, cognitive bias, changing patient expectations, and institutional pressure to produce closure. Drawing on literature concerning telemedicine, risk communication, cyberchondria, overdiagnosis, shared decision-making, and artificial intelligence, the paper argues that digital environments can shift thresholds for consultation, testing, reassurance, and referral without directly determining any single clinical outcome. Remote care may increase uncertainty when examination is limited; online information may increase perceived certainty before consultation; and both conditions can converge in ways that favor exclusion-oriented testing. Legal and organizational responsibility is likewise complicated when clinical decisions depend on infrastructures, interfaces, and externally formed diagnostic expectations. The article proposes a practical framework centered on modality sufficiency, proportional risk communication, traceability, institutional accountability, and uncertainty-oriented health literacy. Digital medicine is therefore best understood neither as a threat to clinical judgment nor as a neutral extension of conventional care, but as an environment that changes the informational conditions in which judgment is exercised.

title: Towards Street Oceanography: Ginza Street as a Case Study

detail.title: Towards Street Oceanography: Ginza Street as a Case Study
detail.abstract:
A companion paper proposes a field organised around the street understood as an open system: heterogeneous flows passing through a heterogeneous terrain, forced from outside on several timescales, altering what passes through and altered in turn. That proposal was made in the abstract, and a proposal for a field earns attention only where its questions have determinate content on an actual street and records adequate to answer them can be shown to exist. Supplying that demonstration is the role of this paper. 

      The case is Ginza, in central Tokyo, chosen for three properties the proposal requires of a case: unlike regimes of price, provenance and use within a few hundred metres; a documented arrangement altering the traversable configuration reversibly and on a schedule; and an observational and institutional record reaching back a century and more. The paper sets out that record, reads the district as an ordered sequence of layers laid down since the seventeenth century, and works the field's principal questions through the case in turn. Four findings are claimed. An imposed terrain of the 1870s was documented as initially rejected by its occupants, which is a recorded instance of flow and terrain moving against one another. The interruptions in the record arrive with their causes separately documented, which is the condition under which an absent interval becomes usable evidence. A rule governing the street was made to track daylight, exhibiting an institutional reading that follows a forcing the institution leaves untouched. And the persistence most likely to impress an observer proves the evidence least able to discriminate, since the standing null account produces the same appearance. The paper closes by specifying a first campaign of measurement in four pieces, ordered by what each requires of the others.

title: Local Financing of Continuous Coastal Protection under Fragmented Ownership

detail.title: Local Financing of Continuous Coastal Protection under Fragmented Ownership
detail.abstract: Coastal protection against sea-level rise and storm surge may be planned as one continuous line but delivered by separate landowners. Even with positive aggregate private surplus, the line can remain unfinanceable when parcels with available participation margin are ineligible to fund a costly interface. This paper characterises that constraint under a fixed assessment rule. Parcels form a path, receive private value only when the full line is documented as complete, and may finance an interface only within a specified payer radius. A radius-specific allocation supports full completion as a Nash equilibrium if and only if every parcel has a non-negative participation margin and every contiguous block of interfaces costs no more than the participation margin in its expanded payer neighbourhood. The condition identifies the maximum block deficit and the minimum feasible payer radius. The model distinguishes the problems of a negative parcel margin, an aggregate private deficit, a spatially inaccessible margin, and equilibrium selection. Signed transfers address the first; outside finance covers the second when external value makes completion socially worthwhile; broader incidence addresses the third. Commitment, not transfers, addresses the fourth: completion-contingent transfers do not remove the no-build equilibrium unless commitment changes the payoff from non-participation. Singapore, a low-lying island state building continuous coastal defences across separately owned land, provides the physical and institutional setting.

title: Street Oceanography: An Oceanographic Epistemology of Socio-Cultural Dynamical Systems - Preliminary Discussion

detail.title: Street Oceanography: An Oceanographic Epistemology of Socio-Cultural Dynamical Systems - Preliminary Discussion
detail.abstract: A street is studied at present as a physical form, a transport link, a commercial location, a public space, a social setting, and a cultural landscape. Each description is well developed, and each treats as background what another treats as its object, which leaves the composite object without a field of its own. This paper gives a preliminary account of the foundations such a field would require, borrowing from oceanography a disciplinary form in place of a set of equations: a field organised around one object, admitting whatever method that object requires, and holding transport, composition, reaction, ecology, deposition and external coupling within a single account. The paper undertakes five foundational tasks. It fixes the object and its boundary, and states the premise of reciprocal alteration from which the field departs, namely that both the flow and the terrain are heterogeneous and that each alters the other. It sets out the discipline governing the borrowing, admitting a feature of the source field where it brings a theorem or a measurable, and records the standing of each feature on a graded and revisable scale. It identifies four respects in which the object departs from an ocean, which is what indicates a field in place of an application. It maps the field into nine domains of question and nine classes of instrument, gives the correspondence between them, and treats the empty cells of that correspondence as the research agenda. And it states the terms on which the proposal could fail, naming five null accounts any finding must defeat and giving the classification by which the field would first be tested. Three further results bear on practice: the obstructions that keep models of this class hard to deploy, the argument that governance reaches generativity only through susceptibility and the conditions of generation, and the distributive and reflexive questions that acting on conditions raises.

title: Trained to Treat Half the Population: Closing Canada's Medical Education Gap in Menopause Care

detail.title: Trained to Treat Half the Population: Closing Canada's Medical Education Gap in Menopause Care

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the Founder and Executive Director of Menopause Matter, the organization referenced throughout this paper. No other competing financial or personal interests are declared.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Menopause Matter self-funded the development of this paper as part of its ongoing policy advocacy work.

detail.abstract: Women across Canada report difficulty finding physicians equipped to discuss menopause hormone therapy accurately. This paper traces that difficulty back to a documented weakness in undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, compounded by two decades of defensive prescribing that followed the 2002 Women's Health Initiative (WHI) study. It maps the institutions that actually control Canadian medical education, weighs competing policy mechanisms against explicit criteria, and draws on both the United Kingdom's 2022 reform and a domestic 2015 precedent to recommend a phased approach: transitional, medium-term, and structural. Every recommendation works through authority these institutions already hold; none requires new legislation.

title: An Overview of Morpho Midnight
affiliations: University of Florida and

detail.title: An Overview of Morpho Midnight
detail.abstract: Morpho Midnight is a protocol for collateralized loans with fixed repayment amounts and maturity dates. It organizes loans into separately configured markets, records standardized repayment obligations and lender claims, holds borrower collateral, and settles trades and repayments through a core smart contract. This paper explains who transfers and controls each asset, how positions are created and closed, how losses are allocated, and what public evidence shows about use of the deployed protocol.

title: A Haptic Teleoperation Framework for Remote Construction: Performance Assessment of Kinematic and Visual Assistive Functions
affiliations: Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge and Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge

detail.title: A Haptic Teleoperation Framework for Remote Construction: Performance Assessment of Kinematic and Visual Assistive Functions
detail.abstract: Telerobotics research in construction has primarily focused on earthmoving, while other important tasks requiring high precision and tracing motions remain comparatively underexplored. Such tasks demand specialized manipulation and feedback modalities to support effective human-robot teaming. This study investigated a haptic interface augmented with assistive kinematic and graphical functions to support efficient and safe execution of such remote tasks. Three teleoperation scenarios were evaluated: a baseline, one supported by assistive kinematic functions, and one supported by both assistive control functions and graphical aids. A human-subject study was conducted to systematically assess operator performance and human factors across scenarios. Both objective performance metrics (task completion time, cartesian trajectory values, and collision counts) and subjective user experience measures were analyzed. The results demonstrate that the proposed assistive functions significantly improve precision (88%), operational efficiency (63%), and collision-free manipulation (75%) during the simulated telerobotic crack repair tasks while also reducing mental demand and improving the perceived usability.

title: Demand-mediated and Socially Embedded Wage Formation in Albania: Productivity Transmission, Migration and European Wage Benchmarks
affiliations: Independent, University of International Studies of Rome (UNINT) and University of International Studies of Rome (UNINT)

detail.title: Demand-mediated and Socially Embedded Wage Formation in Albania: Productivity Transmission, Migration and European Wage Benchmarks
detail.abstract: This paper examines Albanian wage formation by asking whether real wages are more consistent with a demand-mediated and socially embedded pattern than with a clean productivity-passthrough mechanism. Using annual data for 2000-2024, the analysis combines Albanian wage series with World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI) for real gross domestic product (GDP), labour productivity, prices, unemployment, remittances, investment and final consumption. Parsimonious autoregressive distributed lag and unrestricted error-correction model checks (ARDL/UECM), multicollinearity diagnostics, growth-rate models and eventsensitivity tests are used to discipline the interpretation (Pesaran et al., 2001; World Bank, n.d.). The results show that real wages, real GDP, final consumption and remittances share a strong common trend, while measured productivity is highly collinear with output and does not provide a separately stable wage anchor in the short annual sample. The sociological contribution interprets these macroeconomic regularities through migration, remittance-supported household strategies, public-sector wage benchmarks and the formation of European wage expectations. The evidence is most consistent with an Albanian wage dynamic aligned with aggregate demand conditions and institutional wage-setting mechanisms rather than with a clean productivity-led model. GDP is interpreted as a broad demand proxy for domestic absorption, remittances, investment, public spending and external income, not as an isolated causal driver. The paper contributes to European debates on wage-productivity decoupling and embedded wage formation in small open transition economies (Stockhammer et al., 2009; Lavoie, 2014; Granovetter, 1985).

title: Is Self-employment Stressful? Job Complexity and the Strain of Working for Yourself
affiliations: University of Surrey and Case Western Reserve University

detail.title: Is Self-employment Stressful? Job Complexity and the Strain of Working for Yourself
detail.abstract: Building on job complexity and job demands–control theories, we develop a theory of resource-contingent strain to explain why self-employment can either reduce or increase stress. Self-employment simultaneously raises job demands and control, but the extent to which greater control translates into meaningful decision authority depends on job complexity. We test these occupational predictions using the second wave of the Midlife in the United States (MIDUS) study, linking survey data from 3,199 employed respondents to a biomarker sample of 717 participants and a daily diary study containing four salivary cortisol measurements per day. Consistent with our theory, self-employment is associated with 2.3 points higher perceived stress among blue-collar workers, whereas the difference is not statistically significant among white-collar workers. The interaction between self-employment and occupational context is positive across all seven self-reported outcomes; for perceived stress, the estimated interaction ranges from 2.4 to 3.3 points across nine model specifications. Within-person analyses provide complementary physiological evidence: on days involving stressors, blue-collar self-employed workers exhibit a larger bedtime cortisol response. These findings show that the relationship between self-employment and strain is contingent on occupational context. By identifying job complexity and associated decision authority as key boundary conditions, we help reconcile heterogeneous findings in the entrepreneurship literature and clarify when self-employment functions as a resource versus a source of strain.

title: Price Analysis is Necessary for Global Large Projects: And the Market Only Prices Half of What they buy

detail.title: Price Analysis is Necessary for Global Large Projects: And the Market Only Prices Half of What they buy
detail.abstract: Large-project cost overruns are not new. Roughly nine in ten megaprojects have overrun on cost or schedule for the better part of a century, a base rate that has not improved despite decades of reform. This paper argues that the inflationary window that opened in 2021 changed the character of the risk behind that base rate rather than the rate itself, and that the change is legible in prices. Drawing on a census of about 97 megaprojects, each above one billion dollars, active over 2020 to 2024 across more than forty countries, on a focused snapshot of the 24 largest projects now running or committed, and on a live reading of commodity and component prices in mid-2026, it makes three linked claims. First, the world is building an unusual number of the largest projects at the same few years, and a large part of that build is insensitive to interest rates, so the demand it adds cannot be cooled by the standard tool. Second, only a minority of any project's cost, on the order of 10 to 35 per cent, can be laid off in a financial market, and that fraction is smallest exactly where projects are most complex, because the forward market covers the raw commodity and abandons the finished part. Third, when a cost shock can be neither hedged nor passed on, it does not disappear. It travels down the finance chain until it reaches a party that cannot pass it on, and at the bottom it is absorbed by the physical quality of the asset itself. The central finding is that inflation did not create these delays; it exposed a latent design flaw, an incomplete market whose gap is invisible in ordinary times and lethal under a common shock.

title: The Decision Value of Price and Macro Information: Benchmark-Relative Evidence in Multi-asset Allocation using Historical-Vintage FRED-MD Data

detail.title: The Decision Value of Price and Macro Information: Benchmark-Relative Evidence in Multi-asset Allocation using Historical-Vintage FRED-MD Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses financial-market and macroeconomic data and does not involve human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Many asset-allocation processes begin with an economic view and then translate it into positions. This paper asks a narrower question: once price information is used systematically, does adding historical-vintage macroeconomic information improve allocation decisions? We study 112 monthly out-of-sample decisions from March 2017 to June 2026 across 11 U.S.-listed ETFs and organize the analysis around three comparisons: active ranking versus the same-universe equal-weight benchmark (EW11), incremental macro value versus Price-only, and economic trade-offs versus 60/40.

Price-only earns a 15.3% CAGR versus 10.2% for EW11, with 5.0% annualized active return and an information ratio of 0.71; simple momentum rules also outperform EW11. Macro+Price has a net Sharpe ratio of 0.798 versus 0.821 for Price-only. The difference is -0.023, with a 95% moving-block interval of [-0.351, 0.235]. The conclusion on incremental macro value is unchanged in the raw-series and conservative timing checks. Under the conservative convention, the difference is -0.192 with a 95% interval of [-0.659, 0.175], although Macro+Price selections change in about 53% of months.

Macro-only retains positive standalone performance. The evidence is not a case against macro research. It shows that richer information should be credited with incremental value only when it improves an active process that already adds value after portfolio construction, turnover, and costs.

title: Climate Justice & Caste: Problematizing Western Environmental Security Models in South Asia

detail.title: Climate Justice & Caste: Problematizing Western Environmental Security Models in South Asia
detail.abstract: Climate Justice is more than sustainability-it's a raw cry for social justice that shapes climate vulnerability. From Securitization theory to human security paradigms, western frameworks always overlook these raw inequalities. This paper tried to find out how Western environmental security models ignore caste based inequalities in South Asia, framing "security" and "vulnerability" to erase Dalit, Adivasi, and other marginalized realities. Through a qualitative desk-based approach with postcolonial theory, environmental justice, subaltern studies, and intersectionality, the study reveals how state-centric universalism pattern neglect the tangled oppressions of caste, class, and gender, turning adaptation into elite preservation. The analysis demands a reimagined security based on dignity, equity, and community resilience, with caste-aware policies, inclusive governance, and grassroots participation for meaningful adoption. Finally, the research advocates for a decolonizing climate discourse that echoes South Asia's scarred history and amplifies silenced voices in both regional and global governance before inequities submerge us all.

detail.abstract: Background: Illicit tobacco trade threatens tobacco control policy effectiveness by undermining tobacco taxation and health warning requirements, particularly among disadvantaged groups. We examined illicit cigarette or roll-your-own tobacco (illicit tobacco) use from 2016 to 2024 in the United States (US), Canada, England and Australia.Methods: We analysed International Tobacco Control (ITC) Four Country Smoking and Vaping Survey data from 22,603 adults reporting daily tobacco use. Logistic regression models using generalised estimating equations identified factors associated with self-reported illicit tobacco purchasing in the past 6 months and past month.Findings: Past-6-month illicit tobacco purchasing increased from 8.2% in 2016 to 18.1% in 2024. In 2024, illicit tobacco purchasing was most common in Australia (35.8%), followed by Canada (17.8%), England (16.0%) and the US (7.0%). Increases in illicit tobacco purchasing differed by country (country-by-year interaction p<0·001), with the highest increase in Australia (6·2%-35·8%) and the lowest in the US (6·1%-7·0%). Past-6-month illicit tobacco purchasing was associated with younger age (18-24 years, adjusted odds ratio 1·55 [95% CI 1·29-2·86]), male (1·44[1·29-1·60]), minority ethnicity (1·21[1·03-1·41), low household income (1·25[1·08-1·44]), high smoking dependence (1·63[1·44-1·85]), using both factory-made and roll-your-own cigarettes (1·78[1·58-2·01]), past-month financial hardship (1·66[1·44-1·85]), and current vaping (1·71[1·49-1·96]). Correlates of past-month illicit tobacco purchasing were similar.Interpretation : Greater action on both demand and supply reduction to reduce illicit tobacco use is needed, especially in Australia, and may help reduce health inequalities. Funding: US NCI/NIH; Canada CIHR; Health Canada; Canada OICR; NHMRC and ARC Australia; NRF of Korea; UK NIHR; Cancer Research UK.

title:
A Systematic Review on Carbon Markets in the Sundarbans:
Can Biodiversity Gains Coexist with Community Rights?

detail.title:
A Systematic Review on Carbon Markets in the Sundarbans:
Can Biodiversity Gains Coexist with Community Rights?
detail.abstract: The Sundarbans, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the single largest mangrove block on the Bay of Bengal coast is an important focal point for carbon sequestration (e.g., 56 million tonnes annually), biodiversity conservation, and livelihoods for over 4 million people. This review synthesizes 60+ studies to analyze how carbon markets intersect with biodiversity conservation and community rights. An analysis of blue carbon initiatives reveals that they have the potential to finance mangrove conservation and support ecosystem services. Gaps of strong institutional frameworks, such as transparency, regulatory oversight, and long-term ecological monitoring, risk jeopardizing community (Indigenous and local) rights and environmental sustainability. Guided by principles of participatory governance structures, geospatial planning, and policymakers to embed social justice principles into carbon market design. However, future studies should deliberate on these gaps to ascertain that the carbon markets are following the path that would mitigate climate change as well as promote ecological integrity thereby safeguarding the livelihoods of the vulnerable populations in the Sundarbans.

title: Taylor Swift, Tortured Poets, and the Tax Code's Frankenstein
affiliations: Mississippi College - School of Law

detail.title: Taylor Swift, Tortured Poets, and the Tax Code's Frankenstein

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: MC Law faculty research stipend.

detail.abstract: Taylor Swift's songs inspire generations of fans to sing and dance about love and to "shake. .. off" heartbreak. Swift's hard-earned "reputation" for being a savvy music mogul inspires other creative spirits to be "fearless" in their artistic endeavors. But unless these artists are songwriters and musicians, they should keep their "eyes open" when selling their works, as they may see "red" when they discover their tax rates. The simple fact is that a taxpayer's financial ability to live out their "wildest dreams" may turn on their chosen artistic medium. Notably, the Internal Revenue Code taxes the sale of poems differently than the sale of songs. As a result, in most cases, poets will be subject to ordinary income tax rates, while songwriters may be eligible for preferential capital gains treatment. This Piece explores how U.S. tax laws breed "bad blood" between poets and songwriters who sell their creative work products. It then argues that sound public policy requires Congress to take responsibility for the "tax Frankenstein" it has created by articulating consistent policies for taxpayers who sell or dispose of their artistic works.

title: Inference in Infinite-dimensional Families: Shrinkage, Augmentation and Generative Computation
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: Inference in Infinite-dimensional Families: Shrinkage, Augmentation and Generative Computation
detail.abstract: Bayesian inference for a function-valued parameter now comes with computational guarantees as well as statistical ones: polynomial-time Langevin sampling under local geometric conditions (Nickl and Wang, 2024), alongside a hardness result showing that worst-case-initialised local chains can require exponential time even on unimodal posteriors (Bandeira et al., 2023). The positive result is conditional on an initialiser it does not supply; the negative one says local methods generally cannot supply it. We ask what four tools (global-local shrinkage, latentscale augmentation, generative Bayesian computation, and conformal calibration) contribute at that boundary, and answer with computation rather than advocacy. Two fail. Shrinkage gives no contraction advantage over a level-scaled Gaussian prior even for an exactly 7-sparse conductivity, the paired risk difference being 0.008 ± 0.007 against a between-dataset spread twenty times larger; and the free-energy barrier is dissolved by the unknown global scale rather than by heavy tails, so a plain hierarchical Gaussian beats the horseshoe tenfold in hitting time. Two succeed. A generative quantile network trained on 2 000 forward solves lands above the fifth percentile of the equilibrium log-posterior, computing the initialiser the theory postulates, where cold-started MALA fails at every step size with a deficit of 2 000 nats; and split-conformal calibration of the forward quantity holds 97% coverage under noise misspecification that drops credible bands to 64%. A composition theorem reduces the warm-start problem to an approximation bound on the learned map rather than an isoperimetric one, which matters, since approximation theory is not what the hardness results obstruct.

title: Eco-capitalism or Greenwashing? Analyzing the Political Economy of Carbon Markets and their Impact on Global Inequality

detail.title: Eco-capitalism or Greenwashing? Analyzing the Political Economy of Carbon Markets and their Impact on Global Inequality
detail.abstract: With CO₂ concentrations exceeding 420 parts per million and unmitigated climate change costs estimated at five to twenty percent of global GDP, carbon markets have become central to international climate governance. This paper asks whether these mechanisms deliver genuine emissions reductions or function as structural greenwashing, enabling wealthy states and corporations to avoid systemic change. Drawing on political economy and environmental justice theory, the study applies comparative case analysis to the EU Emissions Trading System, California's cap-and-trade programme, and carbon offset dynamics in sub-Saharan Africa. The EU ETS cut covered-sector emissions by 37 percent between 2005 and 2022 under stringent conditions, yet such governance remains structurally exceptional. Where caps are weak and offset integrity limited, markets deepen inequalities, reproduce colonial extraction patterns, and generate gender-inequitable outcomes. Examining environmental effectiveness and distributive justice in conjunction, the paper advances a political economy framework foregrounding power asymmetries and structural inequality, concluding with recommendations for justice-centred reform integrating market mechanisms with direct regulation and redistributive fiscal policy.

title: Monetary Policy and Bank Risk-taking under Capital and Liquidity Regulation
affiliations: University of Liverpool Management School and Wilfrid Laurier University

detail.title: Monetary Policy and Bank Risk-taking under Capital and Liquidity Regulation

declarations.funderStatement: BA/Leverhulme Small Research Grants Scheme

detail.abstract: We study how liquidity and capital regulations shape bank portfolios, risk-taking, and asset prices, and how they alter the effects of monetary policy. Private securities are originated under moral hazard and, together with government bonds, back bank deposits. When capital regulation governs the adjustment, additional bonds can crowd out private safe securities and raise risk-taking, whereas under liquidity regulation the effect can take either sign. Capital requirements can dampen and bound liquidity premia. Through the interaction between the two regulations, a larger bond supply can raise the government bond price. Greater public liquidity can also reduce welfare, making welfare non-monotone. Finally, equilibria with different binding constraints can coexist, generating different prices, risk-taking, and welfare.

title: Evaluating Treatment Effects and Replicability
affiliations: and University of Vienna - Department of Economics

detail.title: Evaluating Treatment Effects and Replicability
detail.abstract: We postulate that limitations of conventional testing influence replication assessments. Our analyses are based on a nonparametric, exact test for detecting treatment effects. We first show using simulations and an empirical exercise that this test is powerful. Then, using this method, we revisit 16 studies included in Camerer et al. (2016). We find that eight exhibit an insignificant effect in the original data, rendering replication assessments inapplicable among these studies-yet half of Camerer et al. (2016)'s replication conclusions concern them. Among the eight with significant original effects, seven replicate under exact inference: either the treatment effect is also significant in the replication data, or the confidence intervals across original and replication studies overlap.

title: Adaptive AI Decision Confidence for Resilient Critical Infrastructure Operations

detail.title: Adaptive AI Decision Confidence for Resilient Critical Infrastructure Operations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The author has no personal or financial relationships with any organizations that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, animals, or patient data. All data used in this research were obtained from publicly available datasets (BUSI - Breast Ultrasound Images Dataset). Therefore, no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: A growing amount of critical infrastructure relies on AI-powered decision systems to aid with fast and complicated operational decisions, but these environments are still dynamic and susceptible to cyberattacks, equipment failures, environmental disruptions, and uncertainty in the data. Even though current AI systems are capable of producing quick predictions and recommendations, they might not be able to decide when those outputs should or should not be trusted. This study looks at the shortcoming of traditional AI decision-making, which usually regards confidence as a feature of the model alone, by considering decision confidence as a context-dependent aspect of resilient operations in critical infrastructure. A systematic qualitative review of the available literature was carried out, combining insights from AI decision-making, infrastructure resilience, cybersecurity, reliability, explainability, and adaptive autonomy. The review shows that decision confidence ought to be dynamic not static and that a high level of model confidence does not necessarily mean that there is high decision reliability. The quality of the data, the state of cybersecurity, operational disruptions, and the environmental context can all significantly reduce the effective confidence of decisions made by AI. Therefore, AI autonomy should adjust to changes in confidence and reliability, with lower confidence calling for more human supervision or more cautious actions. The study introduces an Adaptive AI Decision Confidence framework which connects the assessment of AI confidence with contextual reliability and resilient operational decision-making, offering a conceptual foundation for safer and more adaptive use of AI in critical infrastructure settings.

title: Did New York City's Airbnb Ban Lower Rents? Evidence from Local Law 18
affiliations: Berry College - Department of Economics

detail.title: Did New York City's Airbnb Ban Lower Rents? Evidence from Local Law 18
detail.abstract: Cities increasingly regulate short-term rentals in the hope that affected properties will return to the conventional rental market and improve housing affordability. I study New York City's Local Law 18, which requires hosts to register with the city and prohibits booking platforms from processing transactions for unregistered rentals. Using Airbnb listing snapshots, I document the platform-level adjustment surrounding enforcement. Among listings with a recorded review date, entire-home listings requiring stays below 30 nights fell by approximately 87 percent between March 2023 and January 2024, while listings requiring exactly 30 nights became the dominant listing type. I then examine whether this contraction affected the conventional rental market using city-level and ZIP Code-level Zillow asking-rent data and neighborhood-level StreetEasy rental inventory. A synthetic difference-indifferences analysis that closely matches New York City's pre-enforcement rent trajectory yields an estimated first-year rent effect of-0.1 percent, with a 95 percent confidence interval of-2.3 to 2.2 percent. The full post-enforcement estimate is also statistically indistinguishable from zero. Within New York City, more Airbnb-exposed ZIP Codes experience a modest relative rent decline during part of the post-enforcement period, but the effect dissipates and is difficult to separate from pre-existing differential trends. StreetEasy inventory shows no additional increase when enforcement begins. The results indicate that a large contraction in visible short-term rental activity need not produce a detectable reallocation of properties to the conventional rental market or a persistent reduction in asking rents.

title: Hierarchical Meta-regression Analysis of Global Birdwatching Values for Benefit Transfer
affiliations: Department of Agriculture, Food and Environment, University of Catania, University of Catania and University of Messina

detail.title: Hierarchical Meta-regression Analysis of Global Birdwatching Values for Benefit Transfer
detail.abstract: This study provides a global meta-analytic synthesis of valuation studies on birdwatching and evaluates the performance of alternative econometric frameworks for policy-relevant benefit transfer. Using a harmonized global dataset in which the economic benefits accruing to birders are expressed as consumer surplus per person per day, we compare single-level benchmark regressions with frequentist and Bayesian hierarchical meta-regression models that explicitly account for clustered valuation data. Model performance is assessed through leave-one-study-out cross-validation. Results indicate that single-level models perform poorly in out-of-sample prediction and tend to underestimate uncertainty. Frequentist multilevel models enhance inferential consistency but remain vulnerable to sparse and unbalanced clustering. Conversely, a Bayesian three-level hierarchical model estimated using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation provides more stable variance decomposition and significantly lower transfer errors in policy-relevant validation. These findings show that accounting for hierarchical dependence is necessary but not sufficient for credible benefit transfer, as predictive reliability depends critically on how weakly identified hierarchical variance components are estimated and propagated into out-of-sample predictions.

title: Phantom fairness: a reproducible audit of instance-dependent label noise as a hidden source of demographic bias in chest radiograph classifiers
affiliations: , Tata Consultancy Services, Deloitte Consulting LLP and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Phantom fairness: a reproducible audit of instance-dependent label noise as a hidden source of demographic bias in chest radiograph classifiers
detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Deep chest radiograph classifiers trained on NIH ChestX-ray14 often appear demographically fair, although their labels are mined automatically from radiology reports. We test whether this apparent fairness is an artefact of label generation and identify the responsible noise mechanism.Methods: We built a reproducible, CPU-only audit using frozen embeddings (TorchXRayVision DenseNet-121, ResNet-50, CLIP) with per-finding logistic heads. Identical NIH images were scored against three label regimes: NLP-mined, radiologist-adjudicated (n=4,376), and PadChest (Spain, n=24, exploratory), with patient-disjoint splits and the noisy-versus-clean contrast confined to the same images. We estimated subgroup flip rates, applied the Wang-Liu-Levy (2021) group-dependent noise decomposition, and ran a controlled experiment contrasting class-conditional and instance-dependent noise injection, with bootstrap intervals and Benjamini-Hochberg correction.Results: NLP-missed positives were systematically the model's hardest cases (median rank-biserial 0.20, maximum adjusted p 0.014), replicated on backbones never exposed to the clean labels (median 0.16), establishing instance-dependent rather than class-conditional noise. Injecting the measured marginal noise at the lowest-scored positives reproduced the fairness illusion (median 0.081) whereas random injection did not (0.057). A subgroup-specific threshold remedy could be targeted only where the disparity was visible on adjudicated labels, so mitigation depended on a clean audit set.Conclusions: Convenience labels can manufacture phantom fairness through instance-dependent noise; fairness reports built on automatically extracted labels may therefore certify inequitable models. Reproducible, CPU-only auditing against curated reference labels offers a practical safeguard for clinical-imaging AI.

title: ESG Frameworks and Primary-care-Amenable Child Mortality: A Global Multi-method Assessment
affiliations: University of Foggia, , Lum University Giuseppe Degennaro, Niccolò Cusano University, Lum University Giuseppe Degennaro and Lum University Giuseppe Degennaro - Lum Enterprise s.r.l.

detail.title: ESG Frameworks and Primary-care-Amenable Child Mortality: A Global Multi-method Assessment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Author AL was employed by LUM Enterprise s.r.l. The remaining authors declare that the research was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors declare that no financial support was received for the research, authorship, or publication of this article.

detail.abstract: Environmental, Social and Governance frameworks are increasingly invoked in health policy, yet their three pillars are almost always studied in isolation and rarely against outcomes that primary care can influence. Using the World Bank Sovereign ESG Data Portal, this study decomposes the determinants of under-five mortality-the canonical primary-care-sensitive outcome and the target of SDG 3.2-across the full ESG structure. Three equations share the same dependent variable and differ only in their regressor block: Environment (3,533 observations, 174 economies, 2000-2020), Social (2,032 observations, 99 economies, 2001-2023) and Governance (3,592 observations, 176 economies, 2000-2022). Each block is analysed three ways: panel econometrics comprising pooled OLS, one-way and two-way fixed effects, random effects, Between, WLS and dynamic GMM estimators; unsupervised taxonomy comparing six clustering algorithms across eleven internal validation indices; and supervised validation comparing six learners under both random and countrygrouped cross-validation. Safely managed drinking water is the only predictor significant in all six static estimators including two-way fixed effects, with a ten-point coverage increase associated with 21% lower mortality within countries, while particulate exposure is robust on both the crosscountry and within-country margins. Institutional quality becomes significant across all estimators only after the four Worldwide Governance Indicators, correlated between 0.80 and 0.94, are orthogonaliseda collinearity independently confirmed by unsupervised dimension reduction and by out-of-fold permutation importance. Within-country explanatory power ranks governance ahead of social and environmental blocks, while out-of-sample prediction ceilings run in the opposite order. Machine learning reproduces the econometric hierarchy, reveals a U-shaped renewable-energy relationship and a threshold in institutional capacity, and shows that random train-test splits overstate accuracy by up to 23 points of R² through country memorisation. ESG determinants of child survival are pillarspecific in both magnitude and functional form: service access dominates, institutional quality matters above a capacity threshold, and environmental exposures act through structural conditions rather than year-on-year change.
