declarations.funderStatement: No Funding

detail.abstract: This paper offers an in-depth analysis of the political ideology of Sudan's predominant Islamic fundamentalist group, tracing its historical roots, evolution, and practical application in governance. The research employs a dialogic model of interpretation, integrating rationalist frameworks and structural analyses of political, cultural, and socioeconomic conditions. The paper examines the historical trajectory of Sudan, the rise of Islamic fundamentalism, and the impact of the National Islamic Front (NIF), later the National Congress Party, on state policy and society. The analysis includes a review of Sudan's constitutional and legal transformations, policies influencing economic development, and the ideological schism driving civil conflict, culminating in events such as the Darfur crisis. Tables illustrating demographic, economic, and conflict data support the discussion. Conclusions address the discrepancy between theoretical ideals and practical realities, shedding light on the challenges of implementing religious ideology within a heterogeneous society.

title: Good Housing Booms, Bad Housing Booms: Classifying Local Housing-Market Episodes and Their Macroeconomic Consequences
affiliations: Yonsei University and Bank of Korea

detail.title: Good Housing Booms, Bad Housing Booms: Classifying Local Housing-Market Episodes and Their Macroeconomic Consequences

publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Korea Economic Research Institute Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: How can we distinguish good housing booms from bad ones? We develop a high-frequency classification of local housing-market episodes that separates demand-dominant movements from flow-supply-dominant movements and then distinguishes, within demand-dominant episodes, between housing-service-dominant and valuation-dominant booms. We implement the framework using Korea’s Jeonse system—a lump-sum lease arrangement that provides a market-based, capitalized benchmark for current housing-service value—together with monthly district-level data. Housing-service-dominant booms are followed by higher consumption, employment, and output, whereas valuation-dominant booms are followed by weaker economic activity. Using borrower-level panel data covering 710,000 borrowers per quarter, we show that valuation-dominant episodes are associated with greater household borrowing and lower expenditure. The expenditure decline is larger among borrowers with faster prior debt growth, a pattern consistent with a household balance-sheet channel.

title: Constitutional Capital: Separating Authority from Discretion in Long-Horizon Systems

detail.title: Constitutional Capital: Separating Authority from Discretion in Long-Horizon Systems
detail.abstract: Analyses of institutional abuse, capture and dependency typically focus on actor intent, governance quality or ethical norms. This paper advances a different claim: abuse of trust is not primarily a moral failure but an architectural one. Wherever capital renewal is discretionary, authority accumulates regardless of intention—enabling dependency, behavioural distortion and soft coercion without requiring malice. Where renewal is constitutional, that channel of leverage is removed. Conventional responses—oversight, transparency, ethical stewardship and decentralisation—do not resolve the problem, because each leaves discretionary renewal intact. In such systems, power concentrates at renewal points, converting capital scarcity into implicit authority even under benevolent administration. The paper introduces constitutional capital as a design category in which authority is exercised ex ante through rule-setting rather than ex post through approval, and closes by identifying how such architectures fail: not by capture but by reversion—the gradual return of discretion under conditions of urgency or moral justification.

title: Green Transition, Energy Substitution, and Macroeconomic Dynamics in a DSGE Model for Korea
affiliations: Yonsei University, University of Southampton, Bank of Korea - Economic Research Institute and The Bank of Korea

detail.title: Green Transition, Energy Substitution, and Macroeconomic Dynamics in a DSGE Model for Korea

publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Korea Economic Research Institute Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how macroeconomic and energy-related shocks, together with climate-policy design, affect output, inflation, the energy mix, emissions, and distribution in a small energy-importing economy such as Korea. We develop a small open-economy DSGE model with two types of energy: imported fossil-based (“brown”) energy and domestically produced renewable (“green”) energy. Households directly consume a bundle of brown and green energy, and firms use the same energy composite in production. This structure allows aggregate shocks and policies—operating through the relative price of brown versus green energy—to feed directly into consumption choices, firms’ input mix and marginal costs, and hence inflation and output dynamics. Quantitatively, green-technology shocks are expansionary, disinflationary, and carbon-reducing, whereas UIP and brown-energy price shocks are also carbon-reducing but at the cost of stagflation. For a given carbon-tax path, the allocation of revenues has first-order effects on both the output and the inflation dynamics. Monetary policy mainly allocates the burden of shocks between output and inflation, with only minor effects on emissions. The elasticity of substitution between brown and green energy is crucial for the output–emissions trade-off.

title: 국가 간 전이경로를 고려한 대외충격의 파급효과 분석: 대규모 베이지안 글로벌 VAR 모형 (Spillover Effects of External Shocks through Cross-Country Transmission Channels: A Large Bayesian Global VAR Approach)
affiliations: The Bank of Korea

detail.title: 국가 간 전이경로를 고려한 대외충격의 파급효과 분석: 대규모 베이지안 글로벌 VAR 모형 (Spillover Effects of External Shocks through Cross-Country Transmission Channels: A Large Bayesian Global VAR Approach)

publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Korea Economic Research Institute Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This study constructs a Large Bayesian Global Vector Autoregression (LB-GVAR) model covering eight major economies including South Korea, the US, Japan, China, the Eurozone, Brazil, Russia, and India to endogenously analyze international shock transmissions. The model incorporates four features. First, by applying Bayesian regularization techniques, the number of variables included per country is expanded to a range of 10 to 20, thereby broadly encompassing real, price, financial, and climate variables. Second, an outlier correction procedure prevents distortions in parameter estimation from extreme events. Third, optimal hyperparameters are endogenously determined via marginal likelihood maximization. Fourth, a masking technique isolates direct impacts from indirect network spillovers. Scenario analysis of five macroeconomic and climate shocks reveals that US monetary tightening and financial uncertainty induce global economic slowdowns and disinflation. Conversely, energy and climate shocks create a policy trade-off with simultaneous growth contraction and inflation. Furthermore, masking results show that indirect network effects account for a substantial portion of the total impact, underscoring the necessity of explicitly modeling international transmission channels to rigorously evaluate macroeconomic spillovers.

title:
The Economics of One Earth:
From Rent Extraction to Stewardship, Supply-Responsive Allocation and Bounded Inequality

detail.title:
The Economics of One Earth:
From Rent Extraction to Stewardship, Supply-Responsive Allocation and Bounded Inequality
detail.abstract:
The wider transition architecture may include low-cost voluntary civic mechanisms, such as the One Earth Badge, to build participation and public awareness before institutional change. Their economic significance is indirect: any effects on participation, coordination or adoption should be measured rather than assumed. The economic case therefore remains focused on productive capacity, institutions, allocation and stewardship rather than on any single participation technology.
Project One Earth proposes an economic architecture designed to shift attention from financial extraction toward productive capacity, universal provision, stewardship and bounded inequality. The paper develops a supply-responsive allocation model in which essential goods and services are treated primarily as real-resource questions rather than as problems of monetary scarcity. It distinguishes productive returns from rent-like claims and argues that transition policy should protect productive capacity while redirecting investment toward energy, infrastructure, housing, education, health, logistics, ecological resilience and technological diffusion. A central hypothesis is that sustained productivity growth can reduce the amount of human labour required to provide a high material standard of living. The paper therefore models scenarios around a 2% annual productivity-growth rate, while treating this as an empirically testable scenario rather than a forecast. AI is considered one contributor among several, alongside energy investment, automation, infrastructure renewal, skills, organisational improvement and technology diffusion. Demographic stabilisation is incorporated because declining or ageing populations change the relationship between productivity and required labour hours. The paper also considers candidate development pilots in Africa and other regions as test cases for how investment, education, infrastructure and technology can alter productive capacity. The proposed economic transition is gradual, model-based and explicitly uncertain. Its central research question is whether coordinated investment and institutional reform can raise productive capacity sufficiently that societies can provide essential needs with progressively less compulsory labour, while preserving incentives, ecological limits, individual choice and democratic legitimacy.
The quantitative case developed in Appendix B provides a deliberately conservative stress test: a mature connected system of approximately 60 million residents, around 15 million full-time-equivalent workers, cumulative development capital of approximately USD 60 trillion, and an illustrative mature annual GVA of approximately USD 2.5 trillion. These figures are not forecasts; they are a transparent benchmark against which physical output, capital intensity, construction capacity and institutional performance can be tested.

title: The Thorin Density of the Nakamura Measure
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Thorin Density of the Nakamura Measure
detail.abstract: Nakamura (2015) represents ξ(σ-it)/ξ(σ) as a Lévy-Khintchine exponent whose Lévy measure is signed, with density-2 γ cos(γx) x-1 e-(σ-1/2)x. Lemma 1 of the RH8 note carries a Lévy density to a Thorin density by a sine-squared transform. We compute that transform and find that it is nothing more than a logarithmic derivative: for any f admitting the Lévy form at abscissa α, the Thorin density is U f α (z) = (π √ 2z)-1 Re(f ′ /f)(α + i √ 2z). Applied to ξ this holds unconditionally on the whole critical strip 0 < α < 1 and equals a superposition of Poisson kernels seated at the zeros ρ = β ρ +iγ ρ at heights α-β ρ. We then push for unconditional content in the strip. The family is odd about the critical line, U 1-α =-U α ; it is a Poisson semigroup in the tilt parameter; at the line it collapses to the atomic measure carried by the zeros already there, the off-line zeros cancelling in mirror pairs; its total mass to height T is 2N (T)-4N (α, T) + O(log T); its negative mass is at most 2N (α, 2T) + O(log T), which by Ingham's zero-density theorem is O α (T 3(1-α)/(2-α) log 5 T) = o(T), so for every α ∈ (1 2 , 1) the Thorin density is nonnegative outside a set of density zero and the classical zero-free region confines the exceptional set to heights beyond exp(c/(1-α)). The Riemann Hypothesis is the statement that this vanishing defect is exactly zero. Finally, the companion density from the other normalisation of Lemma 1, U α (z) = (π √ 2z)-1 log(ξ(α)/|ξ(α+i √ 2z)|), is unconditionally nonnegative on the strip, this being Nakamura's characteristic function bound; the two differ by an α-derivative, which locates the gap. Two corrections to the printed Lemma 1 are recorded and all identities are checked numerically.

title: Integration Doughnut or a Hole? Economic Effects of European Union Enlargement on its Eastern Member Countries 2001-2025
affiliations: and University of National and World Economy (UNWE)

detail.title: Integration Doughnut or a Hole? Economic Effects of European Union Enlargement on its Eastern Member Countries 2001-2025

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.

detail.abstract: The European Union (EU) hails enlargement as one of its greatest successes, promising prosperity and convergence. Yet, two decades after the eastern enlargement, worthy economic results are evident, as well as cracks. While accession spurred growth and wealth, it also entrenched structural vulnerabilities-rising debt, demographic collapse and deepening internal disparities. The East was expected to catch up with the 'old' EU countries. GDP per capita has slowly converged, but much of it remains locked in a dependent model, with skilled labour flowing westwards, while financial obligations mount. Using a structured statistical analysis rather than econometric modelling, this paper exposes the uneven realities in the EU membership. Integration has lifted national economies, but widened gaps within them, concentrating wealth and opportunity in capital cities while rural and industrial peripheries lag. Meanwhile, the EU's own cohesion is fraying, burdened by crises, militarisation, policy contradictions and enlargement fatigue. As candidate countries in the Western Balkans and the Black Sea region consider their EU future, important lessons emerge.

title: When Political Islam Becomes the State: Cold War Anticommunism, the Contested Handover of 15 July, and Party-State Formation in Turkey
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: When Political Islam Becomes the State: Cold War Anticommunism, the Contested Handover of 15 July, and Party-State Formation in Turkey

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is based exclusively on publicly available documents and secondary sources and did not involve human participants, interviews, experiments, or the collection of personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This article does not treat the rule of the Justice and Development Party (AKP) as an autonomous political era beginning with the founding of a new party in 2001. It locates the AKP within a longer institutional history: Turkey’s post–Second World War anticommunist security order; the incorporation of conservative society into state strategy; the survival and repurposing of religious and nationalist networks after the Cold War; and the search for a Western-compatible form of political Islam after 11 September 2001.

The article argues that the AKP and the Gülen movement were not components of a single organization. They represented distinct and eventually competing capacities within the same historical ecosystem. The AKP possessed mass electoral legitimacy; the Gülen movement possessed accumulated bureaucratic personnel, educational institutions, media resources, and transnational networks. They cooperated in weakening the old military-bureaucratic center, then fought over the political and institutional space that its retreat created. The corruption investigations of 17–25 December 2013 are interpreted as the moment when mutually accumulated information and kompromat became open weapons. Between that rupture and 15 July, the movement’s displacement into opposition enabled wider oppositional contamination, while anger among victims of the Ergenekon and Balyoz proceedings facilitated a new security coalition around the AKP. The failed coup of 15 July 2016 is analyzed not through an hour-by-hour military narrative but as the catalytic threshold through which this interim reorganization was converted into a new regime form.

The article calls this outcome a contested handover. The term does not imply a prearranged coup, a negotiated transfer, or voluntary surrender. It describes a historical result in which the defeated network’s failed move opened an institutional field that the victorious center actively appropriated through purge, seizure, and reorganization. The Gülen movement’s organizational capacity was severely dismantled, yet the governing technologies associated with closed bureaucratic networks—political vetting, denunciation, loyalty measurement, security dossiers, and the selective use of law—did not disappear. They were reorganized around an AKP-centered party-state.

The argument is extended through fragmented external tolerance and securitization. U.S. priorities concerning NATO, sanctions, and regional security and European priorities concerning migration, trade, and stability opened different corridors for the same government. The expansion of Iran-linked financial, logistical, and intelligence networks did not simply terminate this tolerance. It produced legal, financial, and diplomatic instruments through which Turkey’s route could be recalibrated while the AKP’s usefulness in other fields was preserved. The article does not predict that Turkey will reproduce the Islamic Republic of Iran. It identifies the dual function of “new Iran” discourse as both a regional role and a latent language of threat. Finally, it considers Hakan Fidan not as a predetermined successor to Recep Tayyip Erdoğan but as a falsifiable example of a security-bureaucratic transition figure who could preserve institutional continuity while repackaging the ideological form of the party-state.

title: Sovereign Deals
affiliations: University of North Carolina School of Law

detail.title: Sovereign Deals
detail.abstract:
In just thirteen months, the federal government has announced its intention to assume an equity or equity-like position in thirty-three private firms, an aggressive dealmaking campaign previously unseen outside of war or crisis. Drawing on a hand-collected dataset of every deal to date, this Article chronicles the rise of the sovereign dealmaker, and it exposes the reciprocal risks that the sovereign might govern for profit, or that it might use private forms to evade public law. 

Prior episodes of federal shareholding were expressly authorized by Congress, designed to be temporary, or both. Modern sovereign deals are neither. This Article proposes the Sovereign Investment Charter, a statutory framework governing sovereign deals from negotiation to disposition, to constrain the federal government in its unprecedented exercise of sovereign power.

title: The Benefits of Derivatives for the Investor: Forms, Pricing, Hedging, and Leverage -from Options to Credit Default Swaps

detail.title: The Benefits of Derivatives for the Investor: Forms, Pricing, Hedging, and Leverage -from Options to Credit Default Swaps
detail.abstract: This paper examines the benefits of derivatives from the investor's perspective. It systematises the basic forms — forwards and futures, call and put options, swaps, and credit derivatives from credit default swaps (CDS) to collateralized debt and loan obligations (CDO, CLO) —, traces their historical development from ancient harvest forward contracts through the founding of the futures exchanges to the option pricing theory of Black, Scholes, and Merton, and explains the market infrastructure, including margining and the regulation tightened after 2008 (central counterparties, EMIR, the Dodd-Frank Act). Pricing is developed formally: from the cost-of-carry approach for forwards through put-call parity to the Black-Scholes-Merton model and implied volatility, whose numerical determination by Newton's method and by a closed-form approximation is demonstrated in a worked example. Four fully worked applications quantify the benefits: hedging an equity portfolio with protective puts (cost of roughly 4.5 percent for one year, a floor of about 90.5 percent of portfolio value), the deliberate use of leverage through index futures (leverage of 10 and more) and options (elasticity of about 9), hedging a bond portfolio against credit deterioration with CDS, and — from the option trader's perspective — delta hedging a book of calls and puts with outright positions, including the management of gamma, vega, and theta. The findings cut both ways: derivatives are instruments of risk transfer that can improve hedging, return profiles, and capital allocation (Miller, 1986; Stulz, 2004) — yet their leverage, complexity, and counterparty risk demand methodological competence and discipline, as the financial crisis experience with structured credit derivatives attests (Coval, Jurek, and Stafford, 2009). The paper is intended as a didactic synthesis, not as an investment recommendation.

title: Talk or Deployment? AI Disclosure and the Limits of Text-Based Adoption Measures
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Talk or Deployment? AI Disclosure and the Limits of Text-Based Adoption Measures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The share of S&P 500 firms mentioning artificial intelligence in their annual report rose from 38.6% in fiscal 2018 to 96.7% in fiscal 2025. We ask whether this increase measures adoption or disclosure. Using 9,177 paragraphs extracted from Form 10-K filings, we classify each mention as describing a deployed system, an intention, legal risk language, governance content, or a residual category, and validate the classification against 250 manually labelled paragraphs (κ = 0.66 on the binary deployment measure, against an intra-rater bound of κ = 0.78). Three results follow. First, the increase is driven by firms that began disclosing AI after 2022, and these firms describe little deployment: 23.3% describe at least one working system, against 74.9% among earlier adopters, with deployment accounting for 5.2% of their AI text against 27.3%. Second, among firms already disclosing AI before 2022, deployment paragraphs are flat between 2021 and 2025 while risk language grows fivefold and governance language grows from zero. Third, no text-based measure — neither the count of mentions nor the deployment share — is significantly associated with return on assets or sales growth in any of nine specifications. Corporate disclosure became a weaker signal of AI adoption after 2022: the substantive component did not disappear, but was diluted by language that grew several times faster.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Knowledge Distillation(UMKD):A Lightweight Framework for Sepsis Early Prediction and Clinical Monitoring
affiliations: Shanghai University of Medicine and Health Sciences, Shanghai University of Medicine and Health Sciences, Shanghai Institute of Technology, University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, Technical University of Sofia, Technical University of Sofia, Manchester Metropolitan University - Department of Life Sciences, Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine and Shanghai University of Medicine and Health Sciences

detail.title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Knowledge Distillation(UMKD):A Lightweight Framework for Sepsis Early Prediction and Clinical Monitoring
detail.abstract: Sepsis requires timely and accurate bedside warnings in the intensive care unit (ICU). While large-scale deep learning models perform well, their high computational demands hinder real-time deployment. To address this, we introduce an uncertainty-aware multimodal knowledge distillation (UMKD) framework. UMKD employs an offline multimodal teacher model, trained on structured data and unstructured texts, to guide an online lightweight student model. During inference, the student model operates solely on real-time physiological signals, bypassing the text modality to ensure minimal latency. Clinical texts often suffer from input delays and omissions, which injects semantic noise. To mitigate this, UMKD incorporates a gated cold-start fusion mechanism and Monte Carlo sampling to quantify epistemic uncertainty. This effectively filters out textual noise, enabling the student model to learn deep cross-modal features without inheriting text-induced flaws. Extensive validation on the MIMIC-IV dataset demonstrates that the student model attains an AUC of 0.9063 and an AUPRC of 0.7740, closely matching the multimodal teacher's performance. Remarkably, it comprises only 0.08M parameters with an inference latency of just 0.84 milliseconds. By balancing diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency, UMKD successfully overcomes modal absence and hardware limitations, providing a clinically viable solution for real-time bedside early warning systems.

title: FinTech Adoption and Bank Performance in the Gulf Cooperation Council: Panel Evidence from 73 Listed Commercial and Islamic Banks (2020-2025)
affiliations: and

detail.title: FinTech Adoption and Bank Performance in the Gulf Cooperation Council: Panel Evidence from 73 Listed Commercial and Islamic Banks (2020-2025)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study uses publicly available bank-level and country-level data and involves no human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The paper presents the largest empirical evaluation of the adoption of FinTech and its impact on bank performance in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). Over the 2020-2025 period, we form a balanced sample of 73 Saudi Arabian, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman listed commercial and Islamic banks, which give us 438 bank-year observations. Bank-level financial indicators (ROA, ROE, NIM, Cost-to-Income, NPL, LLP and Capital Adequacy) are based on audited annual reports and Pillar III disclosures; observational gaps are bridged through linear interpolation based on country-year sector medians in the KPMG GCC Listed Banks Results Reports. The FinTech indicators at country level are based on the World Bank Global Findex, the ITU DataHub, MAGNiTT venture-capital databases and central-bank regulatory-sandbox registers. An overall FinTech Adoption Index is built and experimented with its constituent parts. The effects of FinTech on bank profitability, efficiency, risk and capitalisation are estimated using two-way fixed-effects panel regressions with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors, and system-GMM robustness tests. We theorise that FinTech adoption increases profitability and efficiency but narrows net-interest margins, with nonuniform impacts across Islamic and conventional banks and across regulatory regimes. Findings present evidence-based policy advice to policymakers who realise Vision 2030/2035 digital-finance aspirations. This article adds to the work of Kayed et al. (2026), who implemented a qualitative scenario-based MCDA framework to Kuwait, with a quantitative crosscountry complement based on observable bank-level performance.

title: A Refresh of Index Levels: What a 1:10 Rescaling of Major Equity Indices Would Achieve

detail.title: A Refresh of Index Levels: What a 1:10 Rescaling of Major Equity Indices Would Achieve
detail.abstract: This paper examines the rescaling ("refresh") of major equity indices at a ratio of 1:10, using the examples of the DAX, Dow Jones Industrial Average, Nikkei 225 and Swiss Market Index, which in August 2026 trade between roughly 14,500 and 63,800 points. Building on the evidence of the decades-long constancy of nominal US share prices (Weld et al. 2009), it argues that the price maintenance institutionalised at the level of individual stocks through stock splits has a functional equivalent at the index level. The paper derives why index levels grow exponentially for structural reasons-the retention of earned returns on equity, inflation, share buybacks, index maintenance-and systematises the effects of a refresh along three channels: the correction of non-proportional thinking (Shue/Townsend 2021), the defusing of risk perception in media coverage, and the reduction of derivative contract sizes. Three implementation variants are underpinned by precedents (Borsa Istanbul 1997 and 2020; AEX 1999). The conclusion is clear: a 1:10 refresh is economically neutral, implementable at low technical cost and grounded in behavioural economics; a threshold rule at 10,000 points is proposed.

title: Demand-Mediated Rather than Productivity-led Wages: Evidence from Albania
affiliations: Independent, University of Tirana and University of International Studies of Rome (UNINT)

detail.title: Demand-Mediated Rather than Productivity-led Wages: Evidence from Albania
detail.abstract: This paper examines Albanian wage formation by asking whether real wages are more consistent with a demand-mediated pattern than with a clean productivity-pass-through mechanism. Using annual data for 2000-2024, the analysis combines Albanian wage series with World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI) for real gross domestic product (GDP), labour productivity, prices, unemployment, remittances, investment and final consumption. Parsimonious autoregressive distributed lag and unrestricted error-correction model checks (ARDL/UECM), multicollinearity diagnostics, growth-rate models and event-sensitivity tests are used to discipline the interpretation (Pesaran et al., 2001; World Bank, n.d.). The results show that real wages, real GDP, final consumption and remittances share a strong common trend, while measured productivity is highly collinear with output and does not provide a separately stable wage anchor in the short annual sample. The preferred interpretation is cautious: Albanian wage dynamics appear more closely aligned with aggregate demand conditions and institutional wagesetting mechanisms than with a clean productivity-led model. GDP is interpreted as a broad demand proxy for domestic absorption, remittances, investment, public spending and external income, not as an isolated causal driver. The paper contributes to European debates on wageproductivity decoupling and embedded wage formation in small open transition economies (Stockhammer et al., 2009; Lavoie, 2014; Granovetter, 1985).

title: The Limits of Climate Determinism: Weather and Grain Price Dynamics in Qing China
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, National Taiwan Normal University and Fudan University

detail.title: The Limits of Climate Determinism: Weather and Grain Price Dynamics in Qing China
detail.abstract: The literature on the impact of climate and weather variability on the economic andpolitical development of pre-industrial China is dominated by a climate-deterministicnarrative, in which hotter and wetter conditions are systematically associated withlower grain prices and, by implication, higher agricultural productivity (i.e., yields).However, beneath this apparent coherence lie important empirical gaps, rootedin the assumption of a mechanistic demand–supply relationship between harvestyields and price fluctuations that implicitly overlooks the role of societal intervention in the price formation process. In this paper, we re-examine the relationshipbetween climate variability and wheat prices in Qing China by explicitly incorporating societal response into the empirical analysis. Using a two-way fixed-effectsdistributed-lag panel model, we combine previously unpublished annual provincialdata on the Qing imperial granary system with observations on climate variability and wheat prices across 16 provinces over the period 1736–1911 to assess howinstitutional intervention influenced the seasonal transmission of weather shocksinto wheat prices. Our findings consistently indicate that granary storage played asubstantial price-stabilizing role and provided a countercyclical buffer against thetransmission of weather shocks into wheat prices. Consequently, direct weathereffects appear generally more limited and more seasonally heterogeneous than suggested by the conventional climate-deterministic interpretation. Taken together,these findings challenge the uniform and mechanical climate–agriculture relationship assumed in much of the literature on pre-industrial China, highlighting thecentral role of societal agency in shaping the economic consequences of climatevariability.

title: CHiMIL: Clinically Inspired Hierarchical Multi-Instance Learning for Multimodal Residual Disease Prediction after Neoadjuvant Therapy in Lung Cancer
affiliations: Shanghai University of Engineering Science, Fudan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shanghai University of Engineering Science, Shanghai University of Engineering Science, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: CHiMIL: Clinically Inspired Hierarchical Multi-Instance Learning for Multimodal Residual Disease Prediction after Neoadjuvant Therapy in Lung Cancer

keywords.keywords: Lung Cancer；Neoadjuvant Therapy；Chest CT；Hierarchical Multiple-Instance Learning；Residual Disease Prediction；Multimodal Fusion；Domain Adaptation；Uncertainty Modeling

detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Chest computed tomography (CT) is central to response assessment after neoadjuvant therapy in lung cancer, but binary endpoints compress clinically meaningful variation into coarse labels. Continuous residual-disease ratio prediction is more informative. Existing CT-based methods often require lesion localization, segmentation, or fixed-length pooling that only partly reflects clinical reading across variable series and slices. This study aimed to develop a clinically aligned framework for continuous residual-disease prediction from heterogeneous CT data. Methods: We propose CHiMIL (Clinically-inspired Hierarchical Multi-Instance Learning), a weakly supervised framework that represents each patient as a hierarchy of CT series and slices. Built on a pretrained slice encoder, CHiMIL integrates selective instance modeling, representation constraint, clinical-information fusion, joint regression of residual-disease ratio and treatment cycles, uncertainty-aware optimization, and representation-space domain adaptation. The model was evaluated on 107 patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) using five repeated patient-level hold-out splits and was transferred to the public NSCLC-Radiomics-Lung1 survival benchmark. Results: CHiMIL achieved the best overall performance, with a cycle mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.509, a residual-disease MAE of 0.219, and a residual-disease root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.263. Compared with the strongest external baseline, it reduced cycle MAE and RMSE by 21.6% and 14.1%, respectively, and residual-disease MAE and RMSE by 9.5% and 5.4%, respectively. Gains persisted across convolutional, general multimodal, and medical-pretrained encoders. On the public NSCLC benchmark, CHiMIL improved the mean concordance index (C-index) from 0.588 to 0.606 and the mean 2-year C-index from 0.591 to 0.608. Conclusions: CHiMIL provides a clinically grounded hierarchical multi-instance learning solution for continuous response assessment after neoadjuvant therapy in lung cancer. By aligning the model structure with the patient-series-slice organization of CT data and combining imaging with clinical information, it improves residual-disease prediction under limited data, variable-length imaging inputs, and distribution shift.

title: The Influence and Impact of Monetary and Fiscal Policy on Financial Markets: from Business Cycles and Monetary Aggregates via the IS-LM Model to the Policy Mix -and What Interest Rates, Bonds, and Equities Make of It

detail.title: The Influence and Impact of Monetary and Fiscal Policy on Financial Markets: from Business Cycles and Monetary Aggregates via the IS-LM Model to the Policy Mix -and What Interest Rates, Bonds, and Equities Make of It
detail.abstract: This paper systematises the influence and impact of monetary and fiscal policy on financial markets along a continuous chain: from business cycles and long economic waves (Kitchin, Juglar, Kuznets, Kondratieff, Schumpeter) through monetary aggregates and the quantity theory (Fisher, 1911; Friedman, 1968), the theory of inflation and deflation with its forms-creeping, galloping, and hyperinflation (Cagan, 1956), stagflation, and Fisher's (1933) debt deflation-to the objectives, instruments, and transmission channels of monetary policy (Taylor, 1993; Bernanke and Gertler, 1995) and the multipliers of fiscal policy (Keynes, 1936; Haavelmo, 1945; Barro, 1974). The IS-LM model (Hicks, 1937) is developed on a formula basis and demonstrated with a fully worked numerical example: goods market and money market equilibrium, fiscal expansion with crowding out, monetary expansion with falling rates, the liquidity trap, and the extensions to AS-AD, Mundell-Fleming, and IS-MP (Romer, 2000), together with the limits of the model class (Lucas, 1976). and QE evidence (Krishnamurthy and Vissing-Jorgensen, 2011), and on case studies from the Volcker shock through the QE era to the 2021-2023 inflation surge. The conclusion: not the level but the surprise moves markets-and the policy mix, not the single instrument, determines the regime in which bonds and equities trade.

title: Intraday 0DTE Option Order Flow and S&P 500 Downside Risk
affiliations: and

detail.title: Intraday 0DTE Option Order Flow and S&P 500 Downside Risk

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Danger leaves a trace. Depth, mostly, does not. Across 1,027 trading days of same-day S&P 500 index options, May 2022 to June 2026, the opening flow is read through a put-call ratio (PCR) weighted by gamma, the quantity that forces market makers to hedge. A put-heavy PCR at market opening is followed by a weaker return over the next hour and, more sharply, by a higher chance that the hour contains a negative return at all. The second follows from the first, since a lower expected return by itself raises the odds of a fall, and nothing beyond that shift is needed to explain the data. The severity of the effect is another matter. Separating occurrence from depth puts the evidence behind occurrence alone, and what the ratio says about depth fades as declines get larger, disappearing among the worst. Out of sample, a rule built on the signal brings no statistically significant returns, before costs as much as after, and a probability forecast built on it adds nothing to one that ignores it. The contribution is to separate the occurrence of a fall from its size, and information from usefulness. What is left is a signal about risk, not a source of profit.

title: A Falsifiable Native Crystallization-state Chain for Character-identity Streams
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Falsifiable Native Crystallization-state Chain for Character-identity Streams
detail.abstract: NINMENI fixes one normalized character as one NMU identity, one ordered stream position, and one prediction target. This paper specifies Emylton, the native state-andobservation chain used to describe the formation, reinforcement, binding, maturation, and recrystallization of organization along that identity stream. Emylton is not a scalar metric. Its primary object is a five-vertex state K t = (P, G, B, M, R) on the four-dimensional simplex. An organization history Ω, a local directional innovation source, and evidence derived from that history drive a conservative evolution operator Φ. A geometric projection Π * (K t) is combined with a separate snapshot-validity path c t to produce ξ t = Π * (K t)c t. This separation prevents snapshot validity from competing for conserved state mass and makes undefined warm-up explicit. We report the exact production binding EMYLTON-NATIVE-RATIFIED-CHAIN-V2 and its stateful CUDA realization PB-K0. It adds no learned parameters, layers, or organs; preserves one ordered update per valid NMU position; and keeps per-stream state independent when padding makes clocks diverge. Seven registered PB-K0 binding falsifiers passed with no failures. On an RTX 4060 at the registered B = 8, T = 2048, D = 768, L = 12 shape, the ordered core measured a 1.9764 ms median and the twelve-layer chain measured 153.8057 ms. These are component timings, not end-to-end attribution. A frozen 500-step pilot contains 423 pretraining and 77 SFT rows. No row has zero positive crystal mass. Pretraining ξ has median 0.4231 and crystal slot mass has median 0.1670; short SFT rows produce smaller values and 49 rows fall below the display activity threshold while retaining positive mass. At step 500, ξ = 0.5932, mean slot mass is 0.3139, and registered parameters for retention, K1 query, and crystal write have changed from initialization. These results establish revision-bound mechanical operation and observability only. They do not establish semantic meaning, model quality, capability, or validation of every Emylton axiom.

title: Convex Price Interpolation
affiliations: Quantitative Financial Consulting

detail.title: Convex Price Interpolation
detail.abstract: We present Convex Price Interpolation (CPI), a convex quadratic-programming framework that calibrates an arbitrage-free option-price surface directly in price space. The call price is parametrised as a B-spline, for which the no-arbitrage properties-monotonicity, the slope bound, and the absence of butterfly arbitrage-reduce to linear constraints on the spline coefficients. Beyond the quoted strikes the price is extended by a wing built as a non-negative combination of asymptotic tail shapes, butterfly-free by construction. The bodies, the wings, and the calendarspread conditions coupling neighbouring maturities are fit together in a single convex program with a unique global optimum. The fair variance swap is an affine functional of the same variables, in closed form, so its quotes enter that program as additional linear rows and pin the deep wing where the option quotes stop. We demonstrate the framework by calibrating a 49-expiry S&P 500 surface spanning one day to four and a half years.

title: Metaverse Realities: Governance, Virtual Property and Legal Ordering in Emerging Virtual Worlds
affiliations: University of Groningen, Faculty of Law

detail.title: Metaverse Realities: Governance, Virtual Property and Legal Ordering in Emerging Virtual Worlds

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded.

detail.abstract: Facebook's adoption of Meta has moved the metaverse from specialist discussion into mainstream legal debate. Yet the term still describes a loose family of virtual environments rather than a settled juridical object. Some worlds depend on conventional platform infrastructure; others place selected assets or governance functions on public blockchains. This article argues that legal analysis should begin with the institutional architecture through which a virtual world is operated. It develops the idea of a governance stack to identify the contractual rules, software systems, token arrangements, decision-making bodies and public law that together determine a participant's position. The analysis then turns to virtual property, non-fungible tokens, intellectual property, immersive data and cross-border remedies. Decentraland, The Sandbox, Cryptovoxels and Horizon Worlds show that claims of decentralisation can conceal very different allocations of power. The legal task is therefore to identify what the user actually acquires, who can alter that position, and which body of law supplies an enforceable remedy.

title: State Policies, Small Business Valuations, and Evidence from Founding-Era Constitutions
affiliations: , East Carolina University, Mercer University and Mercer University

detail.title: State Policies, Small Business Valuations, and Evidence from Founding-Era Constitutions
detail.abstract: We examine how state-level freedom affects small business exit valuations using a large dataset of private acquisitions. Small business values increase following improvements in freedom. We confirm this using textual analysis of original state constitutions as an instrument. The effect is unrelated to firm entry or transaction volume. Improved freedom also increases buyer down payments and reduces seller financing, consistent with lower perceived risk. Fiscal and personal freedom increase valuations, while regulatory freedom decreases them, particularly in highly competitive industries where regulation constrained entry. Buyers price state policy freedom as a durable characteristic of the business.

title: The South Sea Company, the Asiento de Negros and the Financial Revolution in Britain, Revisited

detail.title: The South Sea Company, the Asiento de Negros and the Financial Revolution in Britain, Revisited
detail.abstract: Price and Whatley (2021) used CAPM specifications to argue that the South Sea Company's slave-trading monopoly under the Asiento de Negros (1713-1743) contributed to the British financial revolution by raising risk-adjusted excess returns for holders of government debt and by increasing central government's primary fiscal surplus available "for securing an empire."  This article revisits these issues from inside the company. It analyzes 41 Company records newly-transcribed from the Shelburne Papers that bear directly on all three claims. First, the Company's own semi-annual accounts corroborate the CAPM results, from the ledger side rather than the market-price side. Second, the Company's King of Spain's General Accounts complicate, but do not overturn, the fiscal-capacity estimate by revealing large, unbooked contingent claims between the Company and the Spanish Crown. And third, a documented sequence of Reprisalia claims against Spain, combined with a near-doubling of Company ship armament between 1729 and 1731, supplies direct, primary-source evidence that supports the military-capacity claim.

title: When the Job Opens Doors to Loans: Bank Employment, Loan Access, and Durable Spending
affiliations: Allameh Tabataba’i University, , Arcada University of Applied Sciences and University of Zurich - Department Finance

detail.title: When the Job Opens Doors to Loans: Bank Employment, Loan Access, and Durable Spending
detail.abstract: How is employment-linked access to formal credit associated with the level and composition of household expenditure? We study this question using the Iranian Household Income and Expenditure Survey for 2010-2023. Households whose head works in banking are substantially more likely to receive formal loans and obtain larger loan amounts than observationally similar households. We then use bank employment as an instrument for formal borrowing. Conditional on the instrumentalvariable assumptions, an additional unit of non-housing credit is associated with about 0.7 units of durable expenditure and 0.1 units of nondurable expenditure, revealing a pronounced durable-heavy spending response.

title: Who Decides Who gets Deported?
affiliations: Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law - Yeshiva University and

detail.title: Who Decides Who gets Deported?
detail.abstract:
As President Trump began his second term, he promised the largest mass deportation program in U.S. history, backed by unprecedented increases in immigration enforcement funding. Yet even at historically unprecedented resource levels, the government can reach only a fraction of the tens of millions of noncitizens now subject to deportation. So this Administration, like every administration before it, must make choices about whom to target—and every decision to deport someone necessarily entails an implicit or explicit decision to deprioritize someone else. But who makes those decisions?

Every modern presidential administration has tried to vest such choices in high-level, politically accountable policymakers through agency-wide enforcement guidelines identifying who should—and should not—be targeted for deportation. Yet these prosecutorial discretion guidelines are frequently ignored by line-level deportation officers and immigration prosecutors, who make the individual decisions that, in the aggregate, produce a de facto policy often diverging from the course set by agency leadership. This misalignment between policy and practice poses a significant obstacle to democratic accountability, regardless of one's views on any given enforcement policy.

This Article offers the first longitudinal, empirical analysis of the prosecutorial discretion policies of every presidential administration in the modern era, surveying vast datasets to evaluate their efficacy. From this analysis, we identify the key features that determine the success or failure of such policies and distill proscriptive lessons to help future agency leaders design enforcement guidelines that align stated priorities with line-level practice, mitigating the risks of unchecked enforcement on the ground.

title: Breeding Pig Trade drives Influenza A Virus Dispersal in Swine Across Europe
affiliations: Utrecht University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Université Libre de Bruxelles (ULB)

detail.title: Breeding Pig Trade drives Influenza A Virus Dispersal in Swine Across Europe
detail.abstract: Pigs serve as a reservoir of former human influenza A virus (IAV) H1N1 and H3N2 lineages and act as mixing vessels for diverse strains, facilitating the emergence of novel IAVs. Understanding the spread and evolution of swine IAVs (swIAVs) is therefore crucial to assess the risk of strains with zoonotic potential emerging. This study uses a phylogeographic framework to investigate the predictors of swIAV dispersal across Europe. All publicly available swIAV genomic sequences were retrieved and subsampled for the ten largest European pig-producing countries. Discrete phylogeographic reconstructions were conducted for H1, H3, N1, N2 encoding genes and all internal gene segments. Our analyses indicate that viral dispersal predominantly occurred from north-western to southern and eastern Europe, with frequent long-distance transitions between non-adjacent countries. We also extended the discrete phylogeographical analyses with generalized linear models to test the association between viral movement and potential predictors, such as live pig trade, pork trade, pig densities, farm sizes, or the geographic distance between key pig production zones. We find that breeding pig trade is the strongest supported predictor of between-country transition events across all segment analyses, while larger average farm size in the country of origin of swIAV strains predicted transition events for five out of ten gene segments. Pork trade and geographic distance did not predict the viral dispersal in any analysis. Our results highlight that farms importing breeding pigs from multiple countries could act as hotspots for reassortment of diverse swIAV strains. Strengthening external biosecurity on farms with emphasis on quarantining breeding pigs, limiting long-distance transport, and implementing a One Health surveillance system for earlier detection of emerging strains, could help curb the rapid spread and evolution of swIAV in Europe.

title: Wildfire Smoke Increases Medicaid Expenditures
affiliations: and University of Central Oklahoma - Department of Economics

detail.title: Wildfire Smoke Increases Medicaid Expenditures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Authors have nothing to declare
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract: Wildfire activity in the western United States has intensified with climate change, but its fiscal impact on public health systems remains poorly quantified. Here we combine 7,373 wildfire records with over 2.2 billion Medicaid claim lines across 11 western US states (2018-2024) to estimate how wind-transported wildfire smoke affects healthcare spending. We construct a zip-code-level smoke exposure index using random variation in wind direction and speed, enabling a quasi-experimental design that isolates the effect of smoke exposure from confounding factors like income or healthcare access. We estimate a 2.5% increase in monthly Medicaid spending for a 1 µg/m³ increase in wildfire-smoke-induced PM₂.₅ exposure, driven primarily by higher costs per patient rather than more patients seeking care. Applying a projected 25% expansion of fire-prone conditions in temperate regions to our estimates implies approximately $67 million in additional Medicaid spending annually, or about $1.6 billion in cumulative additional spending by 2050. These findings, robust to controls for heat, provider availability, housing costs, and COVID-19 severity, reveal a substantial and growing fiscal burden that wildfire smoke imposes on public health insurance systems.

title: Belief Functions Meet Quantum Logic and Pay Visit to Constraint Satisfaction Networks and Free Energy Minimisation: A Mathematical Framework for Coherence-Based Decision Theories
affiliations: University of Bologna - Department of Management

detail.title: Belief Functions Meet Quantum Logic and Pay Visit to Constraint Satisfaction Networks and Free Energy Minimisation: A Mathematical Framework for Coherence-Based Decision Theories
detail.abstract:
Decision theories based on cognitive consistency understand decision-making as the process of constructing a coherent representation of reality, capable of providing a reliable causal map that connects actions to consequences. Rejecting assumptions concerning preferences and utility functions, they single out the quest for a coherent representation as the one single factor driving human behaviour.

Decision theories based on constructing coherence are justified by free energy minimisation and supported by computational network models, but they lack a proper mathematical framework. In this article I combine Evidence Theory with Quantum Logic to offer a scaffolding structure to construct coherent representations. I illustrate this framework with stylised examples drawn from medical diagnoses and the BioTech industry.

title: Market Creation without Market Authority: Ex-Ante Evidence from European Emissions Trading
affiliations: University of Basel - Faculty of Business and Economics and ZEW – Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research

detail.title: Market Creation without Market Authority: Ex-Ante Evidence from European Emissions Trading

publicationDetails.journalName: United States Association for Energy Economics (USAEE) & International Association for Energy Economics (IAEE) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: By extending carbon pricing to buildings and road transport through ETS2, the European Union is undertaking a major policy experiment in market creation. ETS2 overlaps national emissions budgets and technology requirements, raising a general question: when does a legal market govern allocation? We distinguish three functions of market effectiveness: scarcity, exchange, and allocation authority. Completing exchange and allocation authority lowers present-value EU policy costs over 2028-2048 by 25.5%, or EUR 1.33 trillion relative to legal market creation only. Allocation authority accounts for 76% of savings; 88% of member states benefit. Compensating remaining losses requires EUR 6 billion, only 0.2% of ETS2 revenues. Restoring allocation authority raises the allowance price but lowers policy cost, implying that the endogenous carbon price in an ETS is not a sufficient statistic for welfare across institutional designs.

title: A New Design for Circuit Breakers

detail.title: A New Design for Circuit Breakers
detail.abstract: This white paper proposes a new design for circuit breaker mechanism that offers an endogenously determined trigger based on the degree of real-time information asymmetry to replace traditional ex-ante, fixed-percentage thresholds. Traditional circuit breakers can exacerbate market crashes due to the magnet effect and prompt High-Frequency Traders (HFTs) to withdraw liquidity when facing order flow toxicity. To shift the purpose of circuit breakers from ex-post market calming to ex-ante market warning, the white paper operationalizes a Kalman filtering framework to track transaction prices as noisy signals of a latent efficient price. By isolating private signal precision relative to public information precision, the framework quantifies the dynamic level of information asymmetry. The paper offers policy applications, including designing new dynamic triggers based on the degree of information asymmetry and optimizing halt durations for different stock groups. The new metric can also be used to enhance the existing Exchange surveillance practices, and provide another criterion for inclusion in headline indices to help protect market quality.

reference: Minnesota Legal Studies Research Paper No. 2026-43
title: Jury Size and the Blackstonian Tradeoff
affiliations: Università degli studi di Modena e Reggio Emilia (UNIMORE) - Faculty of Business and Economics and University of Minnesota - Law School

detail.title: Jury Size and the Blackstonian Tradeoff

publicationDetails.detailsText: Minnesota Legal Studies Research Paper No. 2026-43
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Minnesota Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The conventional Blackstonian ratio compares the social cost of wrongfully convicting an innocent defendant with the social cost of wrongfully acquitting a guilty defendant. That binary comparison is incomplete when both conviction and acquittal require unanimity because the jury may instead deadlock. The consequences of a hung jury depend on whether the defendant is factually guilty or innocent: it allows a guilty defendant to avoid punishment while denying an innocent defendant the finality and vindication of an acquittal. In either case, the defendant remains subject to the stigma of an unresolved accusation and the possibility of a retrial. We therefore develop a six-outcome Blackstonian framework that assigns separate values to four adverse outcomes: wrongful conviction, deadlock involving a factually innocent defendant, deadlock involving a factually guilty defendant, and wrongful acquittal. The framework shows that increasing jury size does not merely reduce erroneous verdicts; it also converts some correct verdicts into unresolved outcomes. Holding the constitutionally required standard of proof fixed, the analysis identifies conditions under which a larger unanimous jury increases expected adjudicatory loss and explains how prosecutorial selectivity and retrial rates change the comparison. A separate theoretical extension examines how jury size would interact with an error-cost-minimizing standard of proof if that standard were allowed to vary.

title: Regulation Without Enforcement: A Political Economy of Waste Management Failure in India
affiliations: Netaji Subhas Open University

detail.title: Regulation Without Enforcement: A Political Economy of Waste Management Failure in India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research was conducted independently and the author has no personal or financial relationship with any company, agency, or organization discussed in this paper.

detail.abstract: India is one of the world's fastest-growing economies, but still its waste management system faces a profound crisis or challenges yet. India is one of the world's largest hazardous waste producers, unscientific management of chemical, nuclear, pesticide and plastic waste. Despite the formulation of various regulations under the Environment (protection) Act, 1986, but still there was heavy mismanagement of enforcing these laws. There was always a gap between these laws and implementation. The paper analyzes the effectiveness of India's waste management policies and highlights these incidents which have happened for not implementing these laws and propose some policies which our government should take to resist accidents and for saving thousands of workers lives. I will propose these laws which are implemented by other nations like Japan, South Korea, Germany, Sweden and Singapore.

title: Robust Downward-Substitutable Co-Production
affiliations: , The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School, Dalian University of Technology, City University of Hong Kong (CityU) and Dalian University of Technology

detail.title: Robust Downward-Substitutable Co-Production
detail.abstract: We study a co-production problem under joint yield and demand uncertainties, where higher-quality products can satisfy lower-quality demand through downward substitution. We first derive sufficient conditions under which the optimal substitution decisions admit a recursive structure and characterize when source-specific substitution flows can be aggregated without affecting realized profit. To support production decisions with limited distributional information, we then develop a data-driven distributionally robust minimax regret framework with a type-∞ Wasserstein ambiguity set. We formulate regret models under both ex ante and ex post benchmarking structures. For both models, we establish the convexity of the worst-case regret function and develop an exact search algorithm for the ex ante model and a finite-scenario approximation for the ex post model. Simulation studies show that the minimax regret approach generally yields higher out-ofsample profits, lower profit variability, and fewer shortages than the maximin utility and sample average approximation approaches, with its advantages being particularly pronounced when data are limited. The results further show that downward substitution increases attainable profit and generally reduces profit losses relative to the true optimum. A real-world case study further demonstrates the practical effectiveness of our proposed approach.

reference: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade Research Paper No. 26/iKIET/225; i-KIET Issues & Analysis, No. 225
title: The Korea-NATO Procurement Framework Agreement: Significance and Implications
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: The Korea-NATO Procurement Framework Agreement: Significance and Implications

publicationDetails.detailsText: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade Research Paper No. 26/iKIET/225
publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
The Korea-NATO procurement framework agreement would give South Korea, a non-member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), an institutional foothold in NATO's joint procurement and logistics support markets. Korea is pursuing the agreement to overcome the structural constraints of non-membership that its unsuccessful bid for Canada's submarine program laid bare. The agreement would open an institutional channel through which Korean firms can take part in the programs run by the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA), spanning acquisition, logistics, in-service support, and systems support. 

The negotiations are expected to widen Korea's opportunities to participate in NATO's defense supply chains and innovation ecosystem. Beyond the existing export market for finished systems, Korean firms could move into life-cycle markets that generate long-term, recurring demand: ammunition, parts, and materials; maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO); upgrades; and education and training. 

The prospects for cooperation on defense critical raw material supply chains and for joint development in advanced technologies such as drones, AI, and space would also improve, and sharing NATO standards that have been closed to non-members would contribute to interoperability. A procurement framework agreement is nonetheless only an institutional gateway into the NATO defense market; it cannot substitute for the alliance relationships and trust that member states have accumulated among themselves. 

Korea therefore needs a medium-to long-term market-entry strategy that expands localization and joint development with NATO countries and draws on regional cooperation instruments such as the European Union's Security Action for Europe (SAFE) and the NATO Innovation Fund. To make the agreement effective, its detailed provisions and their impact on domestic industry must be examined closely. Finally, by identifying security cooperation agendas in which Korea and NATO share an interest, such as responding to military cooperation between North Korea and Russia, Korea can build mutual trust and strengthen the foundation for a long-term defense industrial partnership.

title: Market Structure, Regulatory Fragmentation, and the Industrial Convergence of the Vapor Nicotine Sector A Comparative Analysis of the Traditional Tobacco and E-Vapor Industries

detail.title: Market Structure, Regulatory Fragmentation, and the Industrial Convergence of the Vapor Nicotine Sector A Comparative Analysis of the Traditional Tobacco and E-Vapor Industries
detail.abstract: The vapor nicotine sector is not simply young, it is structurally absent from the institutional market that governs traditional tobacco. This paper argues that the disposable and e-cigarette market functions today as a shadow economy. A multi billion dollar industry whose largest volume brands remain privately held, opaquely owned and largely invisible to the public capital markets that discipline incumbents such as Altria, British American Tobacco and Philip Morris International. Using a comparative industrial-organization framework the paper traces this absence through three developmental phases. An open source enthusiast era, an unregulated disposable boom and an emerging consolidation phase now underway to show that the sector's fragmentation is not a permanent feature but a temporary holding pattern for capital that has yet to formalize. Regulatory tightening, manufacturing audit and tracking mandates are beginning to force this shadow capital into the open. Setting the stage for a "coming of age", a re-capitalization event in which the private giants currently locked outside public markets either consolidate, go public or are absorbed by the conglomerates that already dominate traditional tobacco. The paper's contribution is this structural account of absence and impending capture from an economic standpoint, a perspective largely missing from the public health centered literature on this sector.

title: From Digital Balance to Verifiable Asset: Designing Proof-of-Reserves Mechanisms for Online Gold Platforms Sasan Hatam -CEO of Zelata Gold Trading Platform

detail.title: From Digital Balance to Verifiable Asset: Designing Proof-of-Reserves Mechanisms for Online Gold Platforms Sasan Hatam -CEO of Zelata Gold Trading Platform
detail.abstract: Retail users of online gold platforms hold a digital balance whose correspondence to allocated physical metal is asserted by the platform rather than demonstrated to the user. Proof-of-reserves (PoR) mechanisms developed for cryptocurrency exchanges appear to offer a solution, but they rest on an assumption that fails for bullion: that the reserve asset is natively digital and that control over it can be demonstrated cryptographically. Physical gold has no private key. This paper addresses that transposition problem. Using a conceptual, design-oriented method, it synthesizes the cryptographic solvency-proof literature, physical-market infrastructure standards, and three regulatory instruments governing backed instruments, and develops a four-layer PoR architecture comprising a physical layer (bar-level identity, assay, independent count), an accounting layer (allocation ledger and segregation), a cryptographic layer (Merkle commitment to the liability set), and a governance layer (independent audit cadence and scope disclosure). The central finding is asymmetric: the cryptographic layer can bind a platform to a published set of liabilities and let each user verify inclusion, but it cannot establish that physical reserves exist, are unencumbered, or are legally allocated. Assurance therefore terminates in a non-cryptographic trust anchor, and the design objective is not to eliminate that anchor but to narrow, date, and disclose it. The framework is normative and conceptual; it is not empirically tested and makes no claim about any specific platform. Four failure modes and a research agenda are set out.

title: Carrots or Sticks? Short-Time Work vs. Layoff Taxes
affiliations: and

detail.title: Carrots or Sticks? Short-Time Work vs. Layoff Taxes

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Cleveland Working Paper No. 26-20
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: While unemployment insurance systems are widely used to insure workers against income losses after separations, it is well known that they can inefficiently increase separations in the labor market. There are two distinct policy instruments commonly used by governments that can counter this known problem: layoff taxes and short-time work schemes. This study provides a search-and-matching model to evaluate which of the two is the better policy tool. We show that if only a few firms are financially constrained, layoff taxes are better because they do not distort working hours in the economy. With a large share of financially constrained firms, short-time work emerges as the superior tool, as layoff taxes cannot deter separations in financially constrained firms. Additionally, short-time work can help provide insurance against income losses to risk-averse workers that constrained firms cannot afford to provide in their wage contracts. Calibrating the model to the US economy, we find that short-time work is the superior policy instrument if at least 27.5 percent of firms in the economy are financially constrained. Finally, we show that combining both instruments can dominate either policy in isolation when sufficiently many firms of both types are present in the economy.

title: Beyond a Technology Lens: Characterizing the Problems Entrepreneurs Solve
affiliations: Harvard University - Business School (HBS), Harvard University - Business School (HBS), Harvard Business School - Technology and Operations Management Unit and

detail.title: Beyond a Technology Lens: Characterizing the Problems Entrepreneurs Solve
detail.abstract: What customer problems do entrepreneurs attempt to solve, and what determines which problems attract effort and capital? We construct the first large-scale database of the problems the startup economy addresses, using large language models to write a solution-agnostic problem statement for each of roughly 90,000 VC-backed U.S. startups, validating them against 331 founder interviews, and clustering them into a taxonomy of 265 problems. Six facts emerge. First, each problem is addressed by many distinct technologies and draws firms from several industries. Second, most technologies are narrow; a few, artificial intelligence among them, span nearly the entire problem space. Third, 68% of problems reflect enduring human and organizational needs rather than transient technological, regulatory, or social triggers. Fourth, capital concentrates far more sharply than entry: the ten largest clusters absorb one-third of aggregate venture capital. Fifth, founders sort into problems that benefit from their own expertise. Sixth, ventures with such founder—problem fit raise significantly more capital. The direction of entrepreneurship thus depends on who becomes a founder and how capital is allocated, not only on what the technological frontier makes possible.

title: Ukraine and Russia: An Ongoing Conflict
affiliations: Universidad de la Republica

detail.title: Ukraine and Russia: An Ongoing Conflict
detail.abstract:
The purpose of this study is to analyse the setting, causes, conditions, and nature of the political, ideological, and military conflict in Ukraine, not only from the country's internal perspective but also from a broader regional and global perspective, taking into account all the parties involved in and implicated by the development of the dispute. The analysis therefore requires sustained reference not only to Russia's interests and positions but also to those of the United States and Europe in relation to Ukraine, as well as to the importance of Ukraine for both sides and for their own relationship with one another.

The conflict in Ukraine, and the balance of interests and power among the major powers surrounding it, have implications that are not merely regional but global. One hypothesis examined here is that the containment of Russia has retained an important place in US foreign policy and has, with qualifications and divergences, received the support of numerous European allies. The European Union and NATO, however, do not constitute a single institutional bloc and do not have identical memberships; their policies will therefore be analysed separately. The problem as a whole will be approached from an analytical and interpretative perspective grounded in the historical reconstruction of Russo-Ukrainian relations and in the comparison of rival explanations.

title: Parliamentary Arbitrage and The Case for Regulatory Policy in Parliament
affiliations: Tel Aviv University and  Tel Aviv University, Buchmann Faculty of Law, Students

detail.title: Parliamentary Arbitrage and The Case for Regulatory Policy in Parliament
detail.abstract: This article argues for the implementation of regulatory policy in parliaments. Regulatory policy is a managerial approach to regulation that is implemented in governments worldwide. Its proponents advocate the use of such tools as regulatory impact assessments (RIA) and urge evidence-based decision making and procedural constraints for policymaking. This approach has so far been focused on the government, the executive branch, while it neglected parliaments. Thus, the application of regulatory policy in and by parliaments has been partial, at best. We claim that the absence of regulatory policy from parliament has adverse effects on the ability of parliaments to adhere to their democratic commitments. It also undermines the goals of the regulatory policy approach, and in unintended and unacknowledged ways, affects the coproduction of primary and secondary legislation. The article shows that a "regulatory policy deficit" of parliament may result in unorthodox lawmaking and rulemaking, which we call parliamentary arbitrage, that is, a strategic behavior that bypasses regulatory policy processes and standards, undermining the regulatory policy approach. In addition, this deficit aggravates existing asymmetries between governments and parliaments in policymaking, constraining the ability of parliament to fulfill its democratic functions: legislation, oversight of government, and public participation in democratic processes. The article concludes by surveying some of the existing regulatory policy tools and explains how their implementation in parliament can help confront some of the above-mentioned problems.

title: Tyrannic Modernity, Schizophrenic Vassalage: The Global Southern Ready-Made State
affiliations: UNED

detail.title: Tyrannic Modernity, Schizophrenic Vassalage: The Global Southern Ready-Made State

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Independent research, self supported!

keywords: Global south crisis of knowledge production

detail.abstract:
This book delivers a fundamental critique of the category of ‘Occidentalism,’ arguing that its contemporary revival in scholarship constitutes an epistemic fabrication. This fabrication functions to pathologize situated critiques from the Global South, thereby preserving asymmetric North–South epistemic relations and obscuring a deeper historical pathology.

To diagnose this pathology, the book constructs an interdisciplinary theoretical framework centered on the figure of the Schizophrenic Vassal State. This political form is produced by two core mechanisms: the Ready-Made Modernity Paradigm—the massive export of concluded Northern institutional and epistemic forms as universal solutions—and Vicarious Conditioning—the psycho-social process whereby subaltern elites internalize a mimetic desire for recognition by observing rewarded Northern models. The cumulative outcome is Ethical Schizophrenia, a fractured collective consciousness severed from its own ethical sovereignty.

The argument is demonstrated through a series of interlocking case studies that trace, via a method of traceability, the devastating effects of this global disorder: the philosophical misrecognition of Japan’s Kyoto School (Chapter II), the historical anatomy of Ottoman–Turkish mimicry (Chapter III), and the (post)colonial mirage of the Arab world (Chapter IV), where the state becomes a guardian of colonial legacies. The book culminates in a typology of pathological statehood (Chapter V), revealing a spectrum that extends from the anxious performer to the silent captive of the rentier cargo-cult.

The analysis achieves its full contemporary urgency in its final movement, where the theoretical framework is projected onto the digital age to diagnose the emergence of Algorithmic Vassalage. Here, the schizophrenic vassal state evolves into a new, silent captivity enforced by the data colonialism and black-box AI of the Cloud Empire. This epilogue argues that the foreclosure of ethical sovereignty is now being perfected not by geopolitical hegemony alone, but by privatized, algorithmic infrastructures that annex human life itself, representing the terminal stage of the Ready-Made Modernity Paradigm.

By integrating diagnostic political theory, psychoanalysis, and intellectual history through a method of traceability, the book demonstrates that the Schizophrenic Vassal State is not a series of local failures but the defining global pathology of our time—a pathology that culminates in the silent captivity of algorithmic vassalage, where ethical sovereignty is foreclosed not by geopolitical force alone, but by the black-box architectures of the Cloud Empire.
